en: In this preface to the *Jiubafang Zhuyují*,

I shall test the eye of the school to distinguish the correct from the deviant, shatter the nesting places of intellectual views, transcend gain and loss, and cut off the path of conceptual proliferation. Regarding the public cases (gong'an) of the past and present,

I shall cause them to emerge and submerge, to unfold and roll up, and to turn with exquisite precision, so that one may attain the great capacity and manifest the great function without the slightest trace of obstruction.

This understanding leads one to the ground of great rest and great repose, a place of stability. It is the thorough illumination of one’s own fundamental portion, the great tongs and hammer, and the opening of the true furnace and bellows of a master.

Skillfully grasping and piercing through the myriad transformations is none other than the "picking up of the ancient" (nien-ku), which serves as the path for investigating the mystery and is the very essential barrier. Since ancient times, there has been no great master who did not esteem this. If...

The ground of principle remains unclarified; as for the realm of phenomena, there is partiality and aversion. One falls into the poisonous sea of liberation, and because the locus of views is biased and stunted, one is unable to lift oneself up.
Even if one were to lift oneself up, one would inevitably produce interpretations based on words, failing to discern the true beginning and end.

This is like Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman, or Xuansha’s lack of penetration, or those who obtained the skin or the marrow at Shaoshi—such people belong to the school that marks the boat [to find the sword]. They are indeed obstinate.

However, regarding the depth or shallowness of one's realization, consider how Fayan took up Deshan’s small-scale sermon: those who are merely chasing after clods of earth will surely find themselves split into two parts.
By briefly citing these few instances, it is perfectly clear whether one has penetrated the meaning or not.
The Great Chan Master Fojian was my esteemed friend. While residing at Zhaihui Monastery in Daxiangguo Temple, he sent a letter to Jiaoshan in which he discussed the *niangu* (ancient cases).

He praised Xuedou alone as being preeminent and constantly took his methods as a model. Thereupon, I thought of the *Chanmen Bafang Zhuyujiji* (A Collection of Pearls and Jades from the Eight Directions of the Chan Gate);
although it is widely circulated within the monastic community, these are all the public cases (*gong'an*) of the authors themselves, and no [commentary] had yet been produced.

Regarding the "picking up and presenting" (nian-ti): when I first resolved to take up the small-scale dharma-assembly and ascend the seat to establish karmic connections, I picked up [this matter] to form a segment of a superior event.
Subsequently, he indeed fulfilled his word.

When the imperial decree arrived for him to be transferred to Mount Jiangshan, several years passed until he entered nirvana. I happened to follow in his noble footsteps; as soon as I arrived at Zhongfu (Mount Zhong), I immediately—
He sought it among his disciples and examined it; he had only finished half the *nien* (selections). Regretting that it did not fulfill his aspirations, he brought it to completion.

He spent several years compiling and editing it, achieving its general outline. It points directly to the subtlety of the Way, and its methods of praise and censure, concession and seizure, concealment and manifestation, and killing and enlivening, all merge with the essential principles discussed previously.
It is intended for those who possess the orthodox eye of the school, transcending intellectual understanding.
[He who] does so shall be rewarded. In the seventh year of the Xuanhé era, he resided at Tiānníng Wànsòu Chán Temple in Tōngjīng.
Inscribed by the elder monk Fǒguò Kèqín. Fójian Qín Chánshī. Fǒguò Yuánwù Qín Chánshī.
Chan Master Fang’an Xian of Zhengjue and Chan Master Shixi Yue of Fohai have both read the *Nianggu Ji* (Anthology of Ancient Cases) by the two Chan masters of Zhongfu.

These two masters are like brothers in the lineage of the Zen school; they have practiced the Way for many years, and their reputations are renowned throughout all quarters, standing out preeminently within the monastic community.
Until now, I had never heard such words of shared resonance. It was my regret that the phrases regarding the "thousand-mile echo" between Yantou, Xuefeng, Daishui, and Touzi remained unheard.
Whenever I would sing, laugh, and compose verses alone, I found joy in dancing by myself amidst the forests and springs.
One day, I went to visit...
The Layman Pingdeng, Duke of Taiyuan, found the *Collection of Pearls and Jade from the Eight Directions: Excerpts and Commentaries by the Two Masters* among his desk items.
After reading several passages, he saw that the mastery of the eminent masters—how they suppress and uplift, roll up and unroll [the teachings]—was fully realized therein.

Since this would serve as a mirror for future generations, it was not right to leave it without a record; thus, he inscribed his reflections beneath each passage, following the words of the two masters.
At the end of these verses, they exchanged lines in mutual response. This Way is said to lie in the subtlety of abandoning sagehood and discarding wisdom.
Recorded by the old monk Fang’an Zhengjue (Zongxian) in the year of Bingchen during the Xiaoshing era.
Chan Master Xinjue Xian received ordination from Shaojue Bai. Bai was the successor of Huangbo Sheng; Sheng was the successor of Huanglong Nan.
Thus, Zhengjue was the fourth generation from Huanglong. He traveled south through the Huai and Zhejiang regions and visited Master Yan at Haihui Monastery.
The Master held him in high esteem, and he took Foguo and Fojian as his teachers and friends. Upon returning to Chengdu, he responded to the call of Chang...
Continuing the mandate of Song, he propagated the Way of Shaojue, which spread extensively throughout Shu. He selected and raised up the pearls and jade of the eight directions.
Several decades later, the Elder Fohai Shixi took this [teaching] with him to the south, eventually residing at Tianting in Jinling, where he also subsequently added his own comments (Zuqing).
Zuqing served Fohai at Taibai and Lengquan, listening to his teachings regarding the origins and applications [of these sayings].

This is most detailed. Now, combining the *nianditi* (critical appraisals) of the four great elders, it has been carved onto woodblocks to ensure its transmission for posterity, serving as a great banner of light for the world.
Dated the day of the lifting of the retreat in the fifth year of Baoyou, respectfully inscribed by Zuqing, the abbot of Shengshou Monastery in Wujiang.
Buddha-Mirror, Buddha-Fruit, Perfect Enlightenment, Buddha-Ocean: A Re-edited Collection of the "Jewel-Gems from the Eight Directions" by the Śramaṇa Zuying, Resident of Shengshou Monastery.
Citing an instance from when Guishan was seated: he saw Yangshan passing before the patriarchal quarters. Guishan said, "If it were Baizhang first..."
The Master said, "My son, you must receive a severe beating before you will understand. Yangshan said, "What about today's matter? Guishan said, "Shut your two pieces of skin.
Yangshan said, "This kindness is difficult to repay. Guishan said, "It is not that you lack talent; it is that I, Guishan, am advanced in years.
Yangshan said, "Today I have personally seen the venerable elder Baizhang. Guishan asked, "In what phrase do you see the former master?"
Yangshan looked up and said, "I did not say I saw it; it was simply that there was no distinction.
Guishan said, "From beginning to end, you are a master. Fojian commented: "Guishan shakes his head and Yangshan wags his tail.

Although head and tail correspond and teacher and disciple are in harmony, they cannot avoid the karmic conditions of raising a child. If one wishes to reveal the style of the Great Quiescence, one must directly..."
He was deaf for three days. Afterwards, he gave a shout. Zhengjue said:
"Under Daji’s staff, Yangshan turned like a jade wheel or a pearl; it was as if the wind blew and the grass bowed.
But tell me, in what phrase did he see that Baizhang was no different? It was simply because of his filial piety."
"His strength was slight.
Foguo Haiyun said: "To be able to inherit the ancestral occupation requires a worthy descendant.
Guishan briefly revealed a bit, and Yangshan immediately threw open his chest, yet he did not realize how he was being spun around by Guishan’s pivot."
"Use it! At the same time, it rolls and rolls at the bottom. Furthermore, where else could it be placed?
[The Master] picks up his staff and says, "Setting aside the ancients for a moment, what about today? [He] leans on the staff and says, "It would be well to let it pass."

Once, while they were drinking tea at Mount Gui, Yangshan was standing in attendance. He asked, "After the Master has passed away, if someone asks about the Dharma-way of our late teacher, how shall you transmit the succession?
Mount Gui said, "One bowl of porridge, one bowl of rice. Yangshan said, "If the former person does not accept it, what then?
Mount Gui said, "An adept monk. Yangshan bowed, and Mount Gui said, "In the future, do not cite this [anecdote] in error."
This is not acceptable.
Fojian took up the case, saying: "Miaoshan was dignified but lacked majesty; Yangshan was reverent but lacked propriety. He then held up his staff and said:
"If Miaoshan at that time had known this family style, his descendants would not have been seen [in such a state]."
[The master] cut him off.
Zhengjue said, "What is it to be respectful yet lacking in propriety?
Otherwise, when a father disputes with his son, Fohai said, "Miaoyan drank a cup of tea and was shaken by Yangshan; fortunately..."
Though old, he was not senile; his vigorous strength still remained. Without employing shouts or blows, he surpassed the functional utility of Deshan and Linji.
If you can discern this, you are a master monk.
[The Master] cited the case of Guishan asking Yangshan: "Setting aside matters of the present for a moment, how was it in ancient times?
Yangshan approached with his hands folded. Guishan said, "That is still a matter of the present; how was it in ancient times? Yangshan withdrew with his hands folded.
Miaoyan said, "You wrong me; I wrong you. Fojian took up this case and said:

"Although Yangshan was skilled at advancing and retreating, and at illuminating the past and present, he could not help but be like Miaoyan sipping the soup from within a steamed bun, or pressing sand to seek oil. Even so, tell me: what about Yangshan?"
[The Master] joined his palms. "What do you think? If you can understand this, your journey as a wandering monk is complete.
If not, it is not that I have ever failed you; rather, it is you who have failed me."
The Clouds of Perfect Enlightenment. Yangshan steps forward and then retreats; he looks up to the ancient and clarifies the present. Why did Guishan say, "To each other they yield"?
"Meeting at the head of the Brocade River, we go hand-in-hand up to the wine tower. One who knows medicine has little illness;
one who knows their lot has little sorrow."
Buddha-Haiyun: "Stepping forward, then stepping back; joining the palms at the chest. Penetrating past and present, facing the situation directly.
While this is indeed beautiful, you must know there is a matter that does not fall within the categories of past or present. If you can speak it, then both parties will not have been treated in vain.
Otherwise, take care not to be like a donkey before and a horse behind."

It is related that while Guishan was seated, Yangshan and Xiangyan were standing in attendance. Guishan said, "Nowadays, those who act in this way are few, while those who do not act in this way are many.
Xiangyan moved from east to west and stood there; Yangshan moved from west to east and stood there.
Miaoyan said, "This causal connection will be like gold thrown upon the ground thirty years from now.
Yangshan said, "It must also be through the Master’s proclamation that this can be achieved. Xiangyan said, "Even now, it is not lacking. Miaoyan said, "Shut your dog’s mouth!"
Fojian took up the case, saying: "Tangshan was naturally enjoying a time when the seas were calm and the rivers clear, yet he stubbornly stirred up waves where there was no wind.
Although 'once a single wave moves, ten thousand waves follow,' throwing gold on the ground makes it sound like mere rubble.
If Yangshan and Xiangyan had been able to guard themselves with care, as soon as they heard Tangshan speak thus, they would have respectfully bowed and departed. Even if Tangshan..."
When the mountain coughs or spits, the wind arises; one must also have no place from which to breathe out.

Zhengjue said: "These three old fellows cannot hold themselves steady all at once. Why? It is easy to open a mouth for the beginning and the end, but difficult to preserve a heart through the cold of winter."
Buddha-Sea Cloud: At Mount Gui, the thread was held in hand; as soon as it was pulled, the entire stage moved together.

One person shifted his body without shifting his steps; another shifted his steps without shifting his body. Were it not for this thoroughgoing "old woman’s" compassion, how could one see the immediacy of the occasion where there is no yielding?
Ultimately, what matter of the ultimate realm is being clarified? Shut that dog’s mouth!
It is said that when Yangshan entered from outside, Guishan clasped his two hands together with his fists interlocked and showed them to him.
Yangshan then performed a woman’s bow. Guishan said, "So it is, so it is."
Fojian took up the case and said: "You must know that if your understanding is equal to that of the master, you have diminished the master’s virtue by half.
Only when your insight surpasses that of the master is one fit for transmission. As soon as Guishan [Muzhou] acted upon the point of a needle, he seized hold of heaven and earth;
Yangshan [Huiji] then unfolded the world within a lotus fiber. But why is it so? Have you not heard it said: 'When the work is abundant, the task is accomplished'?"
"When the water arrives, the channel forms.
Zhengjue said, "When the guest arrives, the host rises; at the ceremonial banquet, they raise their heads and wave their fly-whisks.
Yuezhe invited Fohai, saying, "Where there is such a father, there must be such a son; where there is such a son, there must be such a father. As soon as the father...

"Supporting yourself in meditative concentration, how could you have known that your body was among the flocks of hair? You, too, underwent transformation; unaware, you followed your descent into the feathered tribes.
Among the feathered tribes, there are chicken heads and phoenix tails; among the flocks of hair, there are horse jaws and donkey jowls. Why is it so?
Because you slandered this sutra, you have incurred such retribution."
Once, while Guishan was seated, Yangshan stood in attendance. Guishan said, "Jizi, as for the successor to the lineage within our school these days, what is it like?
Yangshan replied, "There are many who harbor doubts about this matter. Guishan asked, "And what about you, Jizi?"
Yangshan said, "I simply close my eyes whenever I am tired; when I am alert, I sit in meditation. That is why I have never spoken of it.
Miaoyan said, "To reach such a state is itself difficult to find. Yangshan said, "According to my own realization, even this single phrase cannot be used.
Miaoyan said, "It cannot be used for even a single person. Yangshan said, "All the sages of antiquity were exactly like this."
Dongshan said, "That is so. Guishan said, "Many people would laugh at you for answering in such a manner. Yangshan said, "One who understands my laughter is a fellow practitioner of mine.
Guishan asked, "What about when one's head emerges? Yangshan walked once around the meditation seat. Guishan said, "He tears asunder the past and the present!"
Fojian held up his staff and said: "When the string is moved, the tune is known; when the leaves fall, autumn is recognized.
From antiquity to the present, wherever one strikes or brushes against it, the Bird Path and the Mysterious Way allow for the intimate travel of father and son.
Yet, even within a thicket of brambles, there is still a lack of awakening. What serves as proof? Consider this: when Yangshan circumambulated the meditation seat once, Muzhou said, 'Torn!'"
It transcends both past and present. If one were a monk with clear eyes, not a single point could be deceived.
Zhengjue said: "Mount Huayan was too permissive and free; Mount Yangshan was too restrictive and tight.

If everyone understands the teaching through such talk, how could the lineage of the Zen school have endured until today? You must know that in his house there is both simultaneous release and simultaneous gathering.
Only by these means can it be attained. Is there anyone who has studied under Yangshan? [He] shatters past and present. Fohai said:
"In the ancestral gate, where the successor closes his eyes to sit in meditation, he kicks a ball on level ground.
One must quickly fix one's gaze upon it. Two strikes lift it up; three strikes keep it from staying. Even if it stays, it remains as before."
He rolled toward the ball gate.
[The text] records that while Guishan was reclining in his quarters, he saw Yangshan entering; Guishan then turned his face inward and lay down again.
Yangshan said, "I am your disciple, Master; there is no need for such formalities. Guishan made a gesture as if to rise, and Yangshan immediately departed.
He departed. Guishan called out, "Jizi! Yang returned. Guishan said, "Listen as I tell you a dream.
Yang bowed his head and made a gesture of listening. Guishan said, "Examine it for me. Yang brought a basin of water and a hand towel.
After washing his face, when Guishan had just sat down, Xiangyan entered. Guishan said, "A moment ago, I performed a feat of spiritual power with Jizang that was no small matter.
Xiangyan said, "I was down below and knew it all clearly. Guishan said:
"Try to explain it to me," [Nanquan] said. Yanguan then brought over a bowl of tea. Guishan sighed and said, "These two sons possess spiritual powers that surpass those of Śāriputra.
Fojian commented:
"To speak of a dream within a dream—this deeply accords with Guishan. As for the wondrous application of spiritual power, it must belong to these two."
Disciple, pass the tea and bring the water. Shining through antiquity and surging through the present, though old in years, my heart remains solitary; I cherish you, my son.
Within the gate of the patch-robed monks, one person stands outside the gate and another stands inside the gate;
yet there is yet another person who has never been hidden throughout the entire world—though the Buddha-eye looks for him, he cannot be seen.
Zhengjue Yun said: "Divine mechanisms and wondrous functions—opening one's eyes to dream; manifesting supernatural powers at inappropriate times to deceive the masses.
Fohai Yun said: "Carrying tea and pouring water; receiving the countenance and responding with words. His wisdom and discernment did not fall short of Śānta;
his supernormal powers surpassed those of Śāriputra. Yet, when examined closely, it is all opening one's eyes to dream."
One day, as Guishan saw a wild fire, he asked Daowu, "Do you see the fire from afar? Daowu replied, "I see it.
Guishan asked, "From where does it arise? Daowu said, "Apart from walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, please ask another question."
Guishan then left it at that. Fojian took up the case, saying: "The blazing wildfire—everyone sees this. Yet only Daowu saw it as utterly distinct.
Stinking smoke and sparks rise from all four sides; walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, there is no contact with it at all. You all..."
"Everyone, you should each take care within the four modes of deportment; do not let him burn off your eyebrows.
Zhengjue said, "I thought Daowu was a man of substance, which is why I asked with such gravity and he responded so lightly.
At that time, had I instead asked him about his walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—how would he have looked at it? And how would Daowu have responded?"
Dui. Master Fohai said:
"The wild fire blazes fiercely; from where does it arise? Purple smoke and crimson flames immediately burn people.
You must know that within sitting, reclining, and walking, there is nothing like seeing it as you use it that is so intimate."
[The Master] raised the case of Guishan asking Yangshan: "How do you understand the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind?
Yangshan said, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars. Guishan said, "You have only grasped the phenomenon. Yangshan asked, "What did you ask just now, Master?
Guishan said, "The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind. Yangshan said, "Can it be called a phenomenon? Guishan said, "Just so, just so."
This is so. Fojian took up the case, saying: "Mount Huangbo was like using a large breast to frighten a small child; Yangshan was like a small child seeing a large breast.
Although teacher and disciple employ each other’s methods and principle and phenomenon run side by side, alas, their spiritual intelligence is one-sided. The discourse continues.
Regarding the term "leakage": only when a man with clear eyes can discern it does he truly know that where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west.
Zhengjue said: "Miaoyan’s question was like striking ice to seek fire; Yangshan’s answer was like [seeking fire] within fire."
A lotus grows. If one deliberates according to the "plain and real" (píngshí) standpoint, both positions possess faults; let us examine this.
Consider, for instance, what Fojian said: "Where human effort does not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west. How can one avoid the faults of partiality and deficiency?
Buddha-Haiyun: Yangshan seized the opportunity with his own skillful means; Guishan followed the error with an error.
Had he not let it pass at that time, he would have asked: "What did you just respond to? Yangshan replied: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth; the sun, moon, and stars."
This too is simply pointing toward the Way. Can it be called "attaining the principle"? Naturally, his wit and skillful maneuvering were such that both beginning and end were perfectly correct.
For example, when Muzhou was conversing with a monk, the monk said, "The rain is truly magnificent.
Muzhou asked, "Where is it magnificent? The monk was speechless. Muzhou then said, "The rain is truly magnificent. The monk asked, "Where is it magnificent? Muzhou—
He then pointed to the rain to show him. The monk remained silent once more. Guishan said, "How can one possess great wisdom and yet remain mute?
Fojian took up the case, saying: "Guishan usually lets forth flashes of lightning from his eyes; yet here, he is caught by the thief and does not even realize it.
This mountain monk is not suppressing the strong or aiding the weak, nor is he partial to principle over kin. But tell me, where is that [thief]?"
This is the den of the thief. If one can identify [the thief] through such investigation, one will be able to mount the thief’s horse to pursue him, seize his halberd, and slay him.
If one fails to identify him, then every word spoken is merely providing the thief with a ladder to climb over.
Today, Zhihai saw injustice on the road. He has apprehended you all along with the stolen goods.
Then, casting down his whisk, he said: "Everyone, identify the stolen property for yourselves."
Zhengjue said, "This monk withdraws himself to yield to others; not one in ten thousand is a Buddha.
Fohai said, "Fujian said that although Guishan usually shoots flashes of lightning from his eyes, when it comes to this point, he does not even recognize the thief.
I, this mountain monk, have observed him from beginning to end: this monk indeed knows how to shoulder his way through and tread upon others' heels, yet he has not yet attained mastery.
As he stepped forward and leaped up, it brought misfortune upon Miaoshan, who lost his money and incurred blame. At that time, seeing what he said— "Where is the good place?"—
he immediately provided him with his rightful fodder, enabling him to have a separate livelihood and sparing him from being censured by those in all quarters.

It is related that when Guishan and Attendant Lu entered the Sangha Hall together, the Attendant asked, "Are all these many monks monks who merely eat porridge and rice, or are they monks who practice Chan?
Guishan replied, "They are neither monks who merely eat porridge and rice, nor are they monks who practice Chan.
The Attendant asked, "Then what are you doing here? Guishan said, "Attendant Lu, you ask yourself."
He looked.

Fojian took up the case and said: "Tangshan was originally of small courage; confronted by this lay official with a single question, he was immediately left at a loss for what to do, flustered and bewildered, closing his doors and locking his gates.
If it were I, it would not be so: I would throw wide the doors and let him in."
When he comes in, this is a Zen practitioner-monk; he is a monk who eats his rice and gruel. You should tell him: "This is a Zen practitioner-monk who has finished eating his rice and gruel.
As soon as his eyes flicker and move, you must immediately exchange them for *mushan* (wooden prayer beads), making him a clear and alert attendant.
If he occupies a high position in the imperial court, he will then serve the sovereign.
When rulers such as Yao and Shun were upon the rivers and lakes, they caused the people to become the subjects of Yao and Shun.
Is this not joyful? Then, raising up his rosary, he said: "Do you all see this? After a long silence, he spoke again.
"This is an old monk who came to the capital and obtained this through exchange. Everyone, return to your respective halls and search for it yourselves.
Zhengjue said: "At that time, the Attendant visited a master; Miaoshan did not wish to force him to know his affairs.
Since the public case had not yet been decisively resolved, he waited until the other asked, 'What are you doing here? and then he could have said: 'Attendant...'"
"Do you still remember the matter of the entrustment at Vulture Peak? If he hesitates, [the Master] shall instead invite him back to the abbot’s quarters for tea.
Foghai said: "In his daily life, Guishan went east and west, striking left and right; today, the Attendant..."
Right before his eyes, why did he wave his hands and kick his feet? The Attendant manifested himself in the body of a high official to stir up and propagate this Way.
How could Mount Guiyan fail to respond to the opportunity presented by his arrival?
If you can grasp it at the very moment he waved his hands and kicked his feet, then you will be able to stand tall and majestic, solitary and remote. *Du!* What kind of talk is this?
Master Guishan ascended the hall. A monk asked, "From the sages of antiquity down to the present day, what is the meaning of the Master's intent?
Guishan said, "What is this thing right before your eyes? The monk said, "Is it simply this? Guishan said, [silently].
"Which one? The monk said, "The one you just pointed at. Miu said, "Which one do you doubt? Do not cause trouble. Fojian commented:
"The question was too perilous; the answer was too grand. Both failed to reach a resolution."
Zhengjue said: This monk asked, "The various sages have continued thus until the present. Guishan showed him what is right before his eyes: "What is this thing?
If that monk had attained awakening from this point, he would certainly have known there is glue within the colors;
what need would there have been to speak of "this" or "that"? Guishan said, "Which one do you doubt? Do not create complications. It was truly unavoidable.
This monk was doubtful.
Fohai said, "From the ancient sages down to those who were ensnared and overthrown by the flying serpent," he cited the monk’s question to Guishan:
"What is the Way? Guishan said, "A mindless state is the Way. The monk said, "I..."
Dongshan said, "It is better to understand that which is not understood. The monk asked, "What is that which is not understood?
Dongshan replied, "It is simply you; it is no one else."
Fojian took up the case and said: "At first glance, it appears as if one is submerged in stagnant water;
yet, upon careful examination, there is salt in the water, and only by tasting it does one know its flavor."
Zhengjue Yun said, "Niurou’s staff is deep.
Fohai Yun said, "Although this monk has no openings, he nonetheless possesses the true cause. Generally speaking, matters of right and wrong, existence and non-existence—"
Whether one understands or not, you and others will always come down to two sides of the argument. This is why that monk was ultimately unable to find his head or nose.
Baoyan’s approach was not like this; how would he have responded to one who does not understand? He would simply say: [The text here implies a direct, non-conceptual response].
"Let it go! As soon as you hesitate, the whisk strikes you across the mouth.
Master Guishan said: "People of the present day only seek to understand directly; they do not realize that what they cannot understand is precisely your Buddha and precisely your mind.
If you seek outwardly for some knowledge or understanding and take that to be the Way of Chan, there is no connection at all. This is called..."
"Carrying manure in is not called carrying manure out; it defiles your mind-field, and for that reason, it is not the Way.
Fojian took up the case and said: "Miaoyan was like a servant before the imperial carriage wrestling with a cowherd boy;

they rose together and fell together, with neither winning nor losing. To the onlookers, their teeth were clenched in frustration as they struggled to reach the bottom—yet it was originally just a child."
"Playful! Is there anyone here today who can act as my opponent? He then raised his fist and said, "If there is one, come forth and meet this old monk.
After a long silence, he said, "Today this old monk has fallen flat on his face on level ground."
The Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment says: "The Elder of Mount Gui was like a great elephant crossing a river; every step was thorough to the bottom.
Nevertheless, he drew in the blind turtle and the floating wood, and the clay ox entering the water.
As for Foguan, who fell upon level ground—who was at fault?"
Fohaiyun: Once, as a profligate youth, he was especially compassionate toward travelers.
He cited a monk’s question to Guishan: “What is the true essence of Baizhang? Guishan descended from his meditation seat and joined his palms.
The monk asked again, “What is the true essence of the Master? Guishan ascended his meditation seat and sat down.
Fojian took up the case and said: "The ancients set up their models and drew their patterns; one could say their heads were straight and their tails were straight.
Yet, alas, all marks whatsoever are empty and false. 'If you see that all marks are no-marks, then you see the Tathāgata.
Zhihai, however, does not do so. What is the true Baizhang? 'Responding to conditions as they arise, there is nowhere he does not pervade. What is [the true Baizhang]?"
"The portrait of the Master. Yet he always sat upon this seat of Bodhi.

Heaven and earth were moved.

Just as before the striking, where was the sound? Each of you should return to the hall and investigate this for yourselves.

Rites and propriety arise from abundance.

Buddha-Haiyun: One step out, one step in; sitting a little, standing a little—exchanging these to manifest the spiritual capacity. What is gained? What is lost? This too is the ordinary state of that house:
the joy of Dharma-delight and Zen-pleasure. Though it is said that worldly airs have not yet been forgotten, how can they fail to shake heaven and move earth?
After all, what matter on the boundary is being clarified? Time and again sold, yet bought back once more.

The Master said, "Because of seeing the seven, one sees the one; seeing the one, one forgets the seven. Yunxia then rose. The Master said, "Sit for a short while longer;
there is still a second phrase remaining. Yunxia asked, "Can one utter words regarding this point? The Master wept three times.
"Go out! Fojian took up the case and said:

Under the blue sky and bright sun, in the second phrase, one attains good fortune because of misfortune. Hanging the sword in the empty hall, go back and come forth;
the words of loyalty and righteousness are difficult to lose. Alas, alas, alas!
The Buddha-Sea Cloud: casting off the body and rushing forward, the guest arrives and the host rises; sitting cross-legged and stretching, the sound accords with its echo.
Because of the seven, one is seen; when a person is poor, their wisdom is short. Seeing the one, they forget the seven; the horse is lean, yet its mane is long.
Rising and departing, he seizes the opportunity to discern the transformation; sitting once more for a short while, there is no room to let him pass. Can you provide a word of comment here?

does the mountain monk still have eyebrows?

that is enough. Danxia said, "This old fellow is jealous; he does not recognize good from evil. The layman said, "You have not yet grasped the master’s case;

"Thread coming and thread going; half-closed and half-open. It is much like two armies arrayed for battle, clashing together until neither victory nor defeat can be distinguished.
They enter the fray once more with spears and banners, nearly collapsing in retreat, yet still there is no winner or loser."
To praise this author: he well understands how to adapt and transform. Today, this mountain monk has no prayer beads in hand, nor does he wield the staff;
there is no one to seize them, nor anyone to strike with them. Tell me, is there still a mechanism for guidance here?
He then raised his fist and said, "If you hesitate, it is not that I have not told you.

I do not know why you expect me to stand beneath your tent [to serve as a page]. Why is it so?
Since you say that he had no prayer beads in his hand, nor did he wield a staff, nor was there anyone to attend him—could this not be a word of cautious reserve?
As for the mechanism of guiding others, how could one ever find it expressed upon a fist? If I were a mountain monk, I would not act thus; I would simply have to laugh "He-he" at Danxia.
"Clearly grasp at the place of great laughter. But tell me, what is it that is being made clear? This group of old fellows are thieves who recognize thieves.

A man who does not recognize pain and itch—if it were not for his aged eyes being sharp and clear, he would surely have fallen into others' pitfalls.
Take, for instance, Danxia’s staff and Pang’s slap: was there any distinction between them as to intimacy or estrangement? Those who know how to recognize pain and itch, try to judge this for me.

Danxia said, "Do not do that! Do not do that! The layman said, "It must be done! It must be done! Then Danxia scooped up some water.

Do you understand? In the end, the water flows toward the vast blue sea; in the final analysis, the clouds naturally seek their mountain home.

Jiaofan.

"This is the father; this is the son. The praise and censure are distinct. *Xu*! Yet there is still a slight difference.
Foguizhai said: "The old man and the boy may be said to have performed similar deeds and thus come to be born in my house.
When Danxia splashed them with foul water, they immediately displayed their thirty-six arts.
It is said that one day Layman Pang visited Ze-chuan. Ze-chuan asked, "Do you still remember the principle [you realized] when you first met Shitou?
The Layman replied, "I am still fortunate enough to have the Master bring it up again. Ze-chuan said, "I knew well that those who have practiced for a long time would become arrogant.

The Layman said, "The Master is old and senile; you do not equal Layman Pang. Ze-chuan said, "We were both there at the same time; how much difference could there possibly be between us? The Layman—[remained silent].

Tell me, does this match the principle of his first meeting with Shitou? Never in a donkey’s lifetime."
When it was time for the tea service, Master Chuanzhu rose from his seat. The Layman then asked, "The Dharma-realm admits no body; do you still see me, Master?
Chuanzhu said, "If it were not for me, I would have been answering with Master Pang. The Layman said, "To have a question and an answer is merely the ordinary. Chuanzhu paid him no mind.
The Layman said, "I did not mean to offend you just now by asking so casually. Chuanzhu again paid him no mind.
The Master shouted, saying, "This ill-mannered fellow! Wait until I present this one by one to those with clear eyes.
Chuandeng took up his basket and returned home.
Fojian commented, "Twice he was left unheeded; he took up his basket and returned home. Tell me, where does the ultimate meaning lie? Do you understand?"
"Do you understand? 'The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip; the sweet melon is sweet from stem to rind. Thus, the old man of Chu has experienced much.
Zhengjue said: 'Master Pang could do nothing with the boat; he had to wait until the scoop was broken.'"
Buddha-Sea Cloud: One person firmly defends, while another attacks with all their might. If one firmly defends, the sea is vast and the mountains are far;
if one attacks with all their might, heaven turns back and earth revolves. Examining this closely, can it be called "not answering the question"?
As Guo'an Chuan was sitting in his quarters, Layman Zhang entered. The Layman said, "I knew only that you were seated upright in your room;
I did not realize a monk had come to visit. At that moment, Chuan lowered one leg. The Layman stepped back three paces, then stepped forward again.
Chuan withdrew his leg. The Layman said, "How free and at ease you are! Chuan replied, "What can I do? I am the master here. The Layman—
[Daowu] said, "He knows only the host; he does not know the guest. Guanzhuang said, "Attendant, serve tea to Master Pang.
The scholar performed a dance and departed.
Fojian took up the case and said, "Master Pang was half-out and half-in; there was a host within the guest. Thus, Guanzhuang extended his leg and withdrew [his hand]."
The feet: the host is within the guest. These two are like dancers; when the beat is rapid, they dance rapidly; when the beat is slow, they dance slowly.
Although there is a distinction between rapid and slow, one must know the underlying rhythm within them. Furthermore, what is this underlying rhythm?
Each must determine it for themselves. Look!
The Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment says: "It is better to dwell in hardship than to practice for pleasure; it is better to be a poor host than a wealthy guest.
Whether advancing forward or retreating back, the source of the matter has been explained. With sleeves fluttering and songs loud, one turns back and departs.
Thus, Old Man Zequan may be said to be well-versed in hosting guests, yet he feels pity for them. As the ritual courtesies are completed, let us have some tea.
Buddha-Haiyun: Where there is a host, there must be a guest; where there is a guest, there must be a host.
If there is a host but no guest, the host’s courtesy is rendered in vain; if there is a guest but no host, the guest’s feelings are difficult to dispel.

Thus, when the Master lowered his feet and withdrew them, it may be said that the host’s courtesy was most diligent; when the Layman went out and then returned, it did not hinder the guest’s lingering affection.
Observing him closely as he performed a dance and departed, one realizes that the profound meaning of pure tea truly intoxicates people.
Master Shengshan called for the layman to drink tea. As soon as the layman received the tea, the Master picked up the saucer and said, "Everyone has their share;
why then do you say you cannot speak of it? Shengshan said, "Precisely because everyone has their share, you cannot speak of it."
The Layman said, "Master, why did you just now say that? Sanshan said, "One cannot depart without speaking. The Layman said, "Quite so, quite so. Sanshan then drank his tea.
The Layman said, "Master, as you drink your tea, why do you not bow to your guest? Sanshan said, "Who?"
The official said, "This is Master Pang. Shanshan said, "If it is indeed Master Pang, why bother to bow again?

Fojian held up his staff and said: "It is like the lute, the zither, and the harp; though they possess exquisite sounds, if there are no skillful fingers, they can never produce them.
Mount Songshan knows how to blow the holeless flute, and Old Pang knows how to play the stringless lute.
Although Danxia responds to the sound and keeps time with the beat, you must know that every beat is a command. If there is anyone among you who understands this, please come forward."
I shall reveal a bit of news to show that there is someone among the assembly; if there is not, then each of you may return to your hall.

Xiaxiang and I have together verified this. It is just as Pang said: "Regarding the matter before the child was even picked up—how, after all, shall we deliberate upon it? Try to judge it!"
The Buddha-ocean cloud follows its current and raises its waves; upon reaching the shore and turning the bend, a single oar-stick is planted firmly.
The Elder of Mount Song does not exert any further effort. When the Layman transmits these words to Danxia, it becomes even more evident that he has brought about his own defeat.

Jushou Shanshan was asked by a lay practitioner (jushi). While seeing the assembly of monks selecting vegetables, Shanshan said, "The yellow leaves are removed;

the green leaves are retained. The practitioner said, "If they do not fall into green or yellow, what then? Shanshan said, "Speak it well! The practitioner said, "It is truly difficult to act as host and guest to one another.
Shanshan said, "Yet you come here and forcibly assume the role of master. The practitioner said, "Who would not [do so]?"
"It is so," said the Master. The Layman said, "It is so, it is so. The Layman said, "It does not fall into green or yellow; yet, within this, how can one speak?

The Master smiled and said, "You too understand how to speak thus. The Layman held the assembly in high regard. The Master said, "The assembly has let you down from the point where your mechanism was triggered."
Fojian took up the case, saying: "If Master Pang had delivered a single turning word at that time, the dialogue would have been brought to completion.

Now tell me, where exactly was his point of failure? Can you all discern it? If..."

you, child-monk without ears, listen closely. Only when the white clouds have completely dissipated will the setting sun shine slantwise upon the green peaks of the many mountains.

One day, while Jushan was sitting with a lay practitioner (jushi), Jushan picked up a ruler and said, "Lay practitioner, do you see it?

The practitioner said, "How could I not say it? Jushan threw down the ruler. The practitioner said, "It has a beginning but no end."

Exert yourself now and you must bring it to completion in this life. What is "seeking weakness within strength"? Where you can afford to yield to others, yield to them.

With the clouds of the Buddha-fruit, one should be generous where there is opportunity for generosity. Look at these two old masters:

If you wish to act according to the full extent of the precepts, you will ultimately fail to reach the point where the ancestral wind sweeps the ground clean.

Had it not been for the Layman who confronted and restrained it on the spot, many would have suffered injury. One person gains the weak from within the strong; another gains the strong from within the weak.

Zhengjue says: "The staff of Mount Song was precisely intended to support the precarious; yet when confronted by Pang Gong’s question, it could not be held fast at all.

"The road is indeed perilous, yet those traveling by night are even more numerous.

He could not help but cry out in grievous distress.

Xixi said, "Old as you are, you still see the faults of others. The practitioner said, "Since I am a fellow student of yours, I ask this on your behalf. Xixi—
Xuefeng said, "If it is so, I shall bring it up from the beginning and deliberate with you. Layman Shishuang said, "You are quite old;

Setting aside for a moment the matter of ordinary daily food, what was the meaning behind Danxia striking the attendant?
What was his intention?"

Jǔběn said, "One might say you have an indeterminate nature. The practitioner said, "This is a matter of the past; one must not speak of the east while pointing toward the west."
Xixun asked, "Regarding matters as they are now, what is it like? The Master said, "Not a single word is uttered. Xixun said, "Before a person of wisdom, such a statement adds so much luster.
The Master said, "Your eyes, Master, are truly large. Xixun said, "It is only by being thus that one attains the teaching of 'cutting off all traces.
The Master said, "One must not allow even a single thing to enter the eye. Xixun said, "The sun is at its peak; it is difficult [to look upon]."
To raise the point, the Master said, "It has already passed right through the skull. Xixian snapped his fingers and said, "Who can discern this?
The Master said, "What extraordinary thing does this old fellow have? Xixian then returned to his quarters.

do not engage with him. Zhengjue said: "The person on the pole is not startled; the person below the pole loses their voice."

One Foot said: "To unfold [the sitting cloth] is the feet; to fold it away is also the feet. Running swiftly is the feet; walking slowly is also the feet.
There is no high and no low; there is no room for deliberation. Tell me, is this the same as or different from Qingshan? After a long silence, he said:
'In the future, do not say that Qingshan Zhihai’s hands and feet were good at helping others.'"
Zhengjue said: "The old man Qinshan showed such compassion as to descend into the weeds; he was far too indulgent, playing with an infant in its swaddling clothes.
At that time, had he simply said 'dada hoho' when the other raised his fist, the latter would have attained awakening and spared himself the need for needless exertion."

Buddha-Sea Cloud: Casting the line and tossing the hook, the intent was for the *kūṇ* and *jīng* (the great sea monsters). When a life was taken and it came upon the hook, what was caught was a lame turtle.
This is the one who is truly eminent; let us deliberate on this further. Then, raising his hand, he said: "Unfolded! The mountains, rivers, and the great earth."
It is firmly grasped; there is no leakage of water. Now tell me: is it opening? Is it grasping?
If you say that both opening and grasping are the hand, then I know you are making a living in dead water.
Regarding Touzi: Upādyāya Fu of Taiyuan came to visit him. Touzi said, "I have long heard of Upādyāya Fu;
are you indeed that person? Fu made a gesture with his palm. Touzi said, "The old monk has been caught. Fu then went out. Touzi said, "..."
Now listen as the various quarters pass judgment. When Fu returned, Touzi struck him.
A monk brought this up to Xuansha, who said, "Was it not Touzi who invited this upon himself?"
Fojian took up the case, saying: "The old man Touzi has a majestic and awe-inspiring presence; his tiger-like gaze is piercing.

He sits firmly, cutting off all access, so that throughout the four seas people retreat in fear of his precipice. Yet, before long, he fell into the pitfall of Elder Fu from which he could not emerge.
How might one deliver this old fellow? Try offering a word."
Zhengjue said, "Fuzhao, you must escort him out with your whole body. Even Touzi’s staff could not fully employ his total capacity.

If one were to judge this according to the standards of various quarters, it would be exactly right; yet Touzi ended up being drawn in. Xuansha speaking thus was also like bending one's elbow so that it does not point outward.
Fohaiyun said: "I thought this was a little mouse that had fallen into the bath; it turns out to be a tiger from within the grass.
If Touzi did not possess the claws and fangs to capture it alive, it would have been very difficult to withstand.
Even Master Xuansha was merely supporting the strong and not the weak."
The Chan practitioner Jurong went to visit Touzi. Touzi said, "I, an old monk, have never uttered so much as a word or half a phrase to catch the ears and eyes of those in all quarters.
Why have you come to see me? The monk replied, "If I were to arrive here and not offer three prostrations, I would simply not feel satisfied.
Touzi said, "A renunciant can be so stubborn and refuse to take note [of the master's teaching]. The monk then circled the meditation seat.
After circumambulating once, he departed. The Patriarch said, "One who has eyes but no ears sits by the fire for six months.
Fojian took up this case and said, "Taking error for error. But tell me, does the guest take error for error, or does the host take error for error?
A man who recognizes good and ill fortune—here, black and white are clearly distinguished; one may walk freely through the heavens."
[The Master] went down to inspect the various quarters.
Zhengjue said, "If I were this monk, I would have simply said, 'Still like this!
Fohai said, "One must discern the specific circumstances and recognize signs of fortune or misfortune; when weapons meet, one who retreats and abandons the field does not understand."
In matters of advancement and retreat, survival and extinction, skulls often litter the fields.
Once, when a monk arrived at Touzi, as he was just about to offer his greetings, Touzi seized him and said, "Do you know that your life and nature are in my hands?

The monk replied, "It would kill me with suffocation! Touzi let go of him and said, "I have cleared your breath for you; I have released your life. The monk said: *Note: The final response of the monk is left incomplete in the source text.*
"Carelessly, I have offended you. The Master said, "When traveling monks go from east to west, they mostly do not meet with the host's approval.
The monk said, "Among them all, the Master lacks compassion. The Master said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice.
The monk said, "It cannot even be avoided. The Master said, "You hired hand!"
Fojian held up the case and said: "Touzi has half a catty; this monk has eight ounces. On the scale-beam, they differ by a mere trifle.
Nevertheless, though it may seem he has gained the advantage, he has actually lost it."
Zhengjue said: "The old man of Touzi possessed a majestic and imposing presence. This monk has consistently been hunching his shoulders and tucking in his feet.

If we discuss 'unfolding the matter' to meet the occasion, where is his compassion? Nevertheless, when worldly affairs are judged by the standard of public justice, human hearts can hardly be made to match the fullness of the moon's orb."
Buddha-Haiyun said: "It is like an arrow piercing the willow tree; if one shoots a hundred times, one must hit the mark every time. If even one shot misses, all hundred are rendered useless.
This monk has just let out a shout at that very moment when the voice was low and subdued. Take it for granted that he shall be settled beneath the bright window."
The story of Zhaozhou’s visit to Touzi is cited: When Zhaozhou arrived at Xiangcheng County to see Touzi, he asked, "Are you the Abbot of Touzi Hermitage?
Touzi replied, "Pay me the fee for tea and salt. Zhaozhou went into the hermitage first; Touzi followed behind, carrying an oil jar.
Zhaozhou said, "I have long heard of Touzi, but now that I have arrived, I see only an oil-seller. Touzi said, "You only..."
He saw an old oil-miller who did not recognize Touzi. The State Governor asked, "What is Touzi?
The miller lifted up his oil jar and said, "Oil! Oil!"
Fojian took up the case, saying: "Zhaozhou held the probing pole in his hand; Touzi carried the shadow-grass with him.
Meeting in the bustling marketplace, both emerged level-headed. Even so, tell me: how was it when they met within the hermitage?
After a long silence, he said: "The clouds and moon are exactly as they were; do the streams and mountains have any difference?"
Zhengjue said, "Meeting under the same canopy; bright moon and clear breeze—why is this so? He added, "Do not be surprised when it is said: 'The world is full of those one knows.
Fohai said, "Zhaozhou merely manages to understand; he embraces a fierce tiger and sucks at its teat, or plucks the pearl from the jaw of a blue dragon."
[The Master] drops the bead. He disregards that Touzi’s life is as precarious as a thread hanging from a string.
[The Master] cites a monk asking Touzi: "The spring rain falls incessantly; why do the hundred grasses not sprout?
Touzi said, "The banana tree simply grows. Fojian adds his comment: "The thunder is vast and loud, yet there are no raindrops at all. The monk asks, "How about this?"
"This is the mystery within mysteries. Master Zhi said, "Last year’s Dragon Boat Festival was like this; this year it is likewise. A monk asked, "Ultimately, how is it?
Master Zhi said, "Therefore, there is neither sameness nor difference; who speaks of before and after? Fojian added a comment: "Two distinct parts.

A monk asked, "What is the second moon? Master Zhi said, "Mid-spring gradually grows warm. The monk asked, "What is the first [moon]? Master Zhi said, "The same as before. Fojian added a comment: "One part is the same."
Yuezi said, "In the first month of spring, it is still cold.
Fojian then picked up the point again and said: "As for Touzi answering him in this way—was he answering his principle (li), or was he answering his phenomenon (shi)?
Is it that principle and phenomenon are unimpeded? It may be acceptable enough to add frost to snow, but to wash soil with mud..."
The Sorrowful Man.
Zhengjue said: "I too was once young and full of charm; now I delight in praising my white hair before my children and grandchildren.
I laugh at myself, sing to myself, and find joy within; do not lock your brows in sorrow for the sake of others."
Buddha-Haiyun: In youth, he once resolved the ranks of dragons and snakes; now old and decrepit, he sings like a child again.
Regarding the monk’s question to Daochang of Lake Zhou: “What is the meaning of the Teachings? Daochang replied, “Disciple, look at them day after day.
The monk asked, “How does one investigate them? Daochang said, “The bright moon spreads across the sky; the forms of mountains and rivers naturally divide themselves. Fujian composed this.
The text says: "Believing and accepting, one puts it into practice. A monk asked, "What is the nature of hearing that does not follow conditions?
Baizhang said, "Try to listen for a moment. The monk bowed. Baizhang said, "A deaf man singing a Hu song; he himself cannot hear whether it is good or bad, high or low.
The monk said, "If that is so, then the nature of hearing is perfectly present. Baizhang said, "A stone standing in mid-air; fire toward..."
"Burning in Water. Master Fojian added a comment: "The moon is bright; it does not exist for the traveler at night.
A monk asked, "How vast is empty space? Chang said, "Too much knowledge arises. The monk said, "I do not yet know what the matter within it is like.
Chang said, "A three-foot staff carries the sun and moon on its tip; a single mote of dust flies up and covers the sky. Master Fojian added a comment: "And blind!"
Beisou Xie. A monk asked, "What is it like when not a single thought arises? Chang said, "A bright mirror stands upon its stand as phoenixes dance;
one does not know that shadow and form are originally a pair. Fojian added a comment: "The thief’s own body has already been exposed."
Fojian further picked up the theme, saying: "The guest is able to cut and polish; the host is able to grind and refine.
One who can recognize guest and host sees the goose as soon as they see the duck."
The Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment says: "The four turning words of the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) must not be treated as mere clichés;

they are like the four seals. One seal is like a stamp pressing into clay—the patterns and colors appear clearly. One seal is like a stamp pressing into water—appearing according to conditions, yet vanishing.
One seal is like a stamp pressing into space—leaving no trace behind. One seal is like gold caskets and jade treasures—not to be opened except by the command of the Great King."
Who would dare look upon this with a direct gaze? If someone can discern it here, one may say that jade and stone have been separated;
were it otherwise, both jade and stone would be consumed by fire.
Buddha-Haiyun: Generally speaking, all questions and answers are nothing other than making a living within the weeds. Only the *daochang* (place of practice) is slightly different. Why?
Because it can lead people into the weeds, and it can also lead people out of the weeds. Furthermore, regarding these four turning phrases:
which one is the phrase for entering the weeds, and which one is the phrase for exiting the weeds? If you can discern this, you will be bright and clear.

The moon spreads across the Milky Way; the forms of mountains and rivers naturally divide. If you do not understand this, it is as if stones were to stand from mid-air and fire were to burn within water.
A monk asked Lingyun, "What is it like when a king goes forth into battle? Yun said, "Guo Pu buried [his father] at Xiong'er. The monk...
[Zhao] Yun asked: "What is it like for Guo Pu to bury [his ancestors] at Mount Xiong'er? Yun replied: "Sitting and seeing the White-Robed Heaven.
The monk asked: "Where is he now? Yun replied: "Do not provoke the Dragon's countenance."

Fojian took up the case, saying: "One discerns the soil from its sprouts; one recognizes a person by their words. When Lingyun saw the peach blossoms and attained enlightenment, his reputation was not in vain.
How does one discern the truth? Have you not seen what he said: 'Guo Pu buried [the bones] at Xiong'er'?"
Zhengjue said: "Once the sovereign has stepped out from his ranks, who would dare to offend the Dragon's countenance?
Guo Pu buried himself at Xiong'er Mountain and sat watching for the 'white-robed' day of the Buddha; he had already offended it."
Fohaiyun said: "This monk possessed the strength to uproot mountains and the spirit to surpass all under heaven;
yet, lacking the mandate of Heaven, he was ultimately captured by Lingyun."
A monk asked Lingyun, "What was it like before the primordial chaos had divided? Lingyun said, "The pillar conceives. The monk asked, "What is it like after the division?
Lingyun said, "Like a single cloud dotting the vast clarity. The monk asked, "As for that vast clarity itself, does it still receive the dot?
Lingyun did not answer. The monk said, "In that case, sentient beings do not come forth either. Lingyun likewise did not answer.
The monk said, "When one has attained a state that is purely clear and free from even a single speck of defilement, what then?
Yunmen said, "This is still the flow of eternal permanence. The monk asked, "What is the flow of eternal permanence? Yunmen said, "It is like a mirror that is always bright.
The monk asked, "I wonder, is there anything further beyond this? Yunmen said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is this matter beyond? Yunmen said, "Shatter it!"
"Jinglai, come forward; let us meet. Foguo held up his whisk and said:

"To reach the state where there is no doubt, to employ oneself until reaching the realm of non-action—where one acts as host and the other as guest, where they press and jostle one another—if one has not thoroughly penetrated the source, how could one enter into such profound discourse on principle? To reach such a field..."
Look at this! In the present age, one cannot even find someone who is like a mirror that is constantly bright; how much less so can one find someone who has shattered the mirror?
Do you understand? Until the cultivation of the mind reaches the ground of no-mind, ten thousand kinds and a thousand variations will flow along with the current.
Zhengjue said: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. They seek one another according to their kind. This monk’s questioning was complete from beginning to end;
Lingyun’s [response] was as if interrupted and then resumed. When it came to the very end, breaking through the mirror to meet face-to-face was just like a lion’s backward leap.
Therefore, Foguo said: 'To penetrate to the point of non-doubt is truly so.'"
How profound! Why is this so? Although the cultivation of the mind has reached the groundless state, it still bears the rosy hue of peach blossoms upon both cheeks.
Fogu Hai said: "Before the primordial chaos was divided, and after it had been divided, thus do threads come and go."
This may be called a profound discourse on the principle. Yet, there were two instances in between where he remained silent;
how then can one provide a theoretical explanation? Even if you were to shatter the mirror, I would still not explain it through for you.
Jingqing raised the question to Caoshan: "Regarding the principle of ultimate emptiness, when there is ultimately no body, what then?
Caoshan said, "The principle is indeed so; but as for the phenomenon, how is it? Jingqing said, "It is just like the principle and just like the phenomenon.
Caoshan said, "You may deceive Caoshan alone, but what about the eyes of all the sages? Jingqing said, "If there were no eyes of the sages, how could they discern this?"
"Not so," said Shanshan. "The official does not permit even a needle, yet in private one may pass carriages and horses.
Foguo took this up and said: "These two elders, within a pit of mud and water, sifted through the sand to pick out gold.
Suddenly they produced a wish-fulfilling jewel. Nevertheless, they only succeeded in discerning 'not so'; they did not yet discern 'so.'"
If you can discern such a thing, then even if a thousand sages or ten thousand sages were to appear before you, they would all have to stand downwind.
But how do you discern such a thing? "In hand, one holds the Vajra-sword that slays Buddhas."
Who asks about Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra?
The Perfectly Awakened One says: "Not so; you are far too groundless. Caoshan was helplessly deceived by Jingqing.
As for suchness, principle, and phenomena—who can fully comprehend them? Ultimately, to be bodiless is also most difficult. Most difficult indeed! This is the eye of all the sages.

Looking back at this, Fohai said: "Jingqing handled the principle; Liaowang acted upon the matter. Cao Shan dealt with the matter; Liaowang acted upon the principle. A beautiful jade from Mount Jing has received the work of cutting, chipping, polishing, and grinding;
it possesses a value so precious that even a city of ten thousand households could not exchange for it. Furthermore, as for the principle of pure emptiness—"
Is there suchness or is there not? Have you not heard it said: "The official seal does not admit even a needle"?
A monk asked Caoshan, "The teachings state that 'the great ocean does not harbor corpses.
What is the ocean? Caoshan replied, "That which encompasses all existence. The monk asked, "Why does it not harbor corpses? Caoshan replied, "Because it is breathless."
The monk said, "One who has stilled their breath does not cling. Sheng said, "Since it encompasses all existence, why is it that one who has stilled their breath does not cling?
Sanshan said, "All existence is not its achievement; the one who has stilled their breath possesses its virtue.
The monk said, "I do not yet know whether there is anything further beyond this or not. Sanshan said, "There is. The monk said, "What is this matter that lies beyond? Sanshan said, "Speak!"
"If there is the Way, you obtain it immediately. But what can be done about the Dragon King brandishing his sword? Fuguo took up the case and said:
"For those of penetrating insight, the great function manifests before them. Their eloquence flows like a cascading river; their minds are like clear mirrors.

Not even a single hair is left unilluminated, and nothing escapes the ultimate discernment. As for the coming of the orthodox and the arrival of the deviant, they are perfectly capable in every respect."
Reciprocity. Although this is a profound discourse on entering the principle, it nonetheless possesses the very core of a monk’s realization.

Yet, among the brothers who inquire today, if one can exhaustively reach the point where breath ceases, that is already difficult to find. Even so, there remains the fact that "the myriad existents are not its function.
Even if one reaches the state where "the myriad existents are not its function," there still remains that which encompasses the myriad existents.
Even if you were to reach the place that encompasses all existence, what can you do against the Dragon King brandishing his sword? I dare ask you all:
what is it to have the Dragon King brandish his sword? I allow only the Old Barbarian to know; I do not allow the Old Barbarian to understand.
The Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment encompasses all existence, yet harbors no corpses. When its function ceases, both inhalation and exhalation are non-existent.
Even if the sun were to grow cold and the moon hot—such words might be altered—the Dragon King would still brandish his sword and the Garuḍa would lose its majesty. Why is this?
Because one house does not know the affairs of another.
Fohaiyun said: "There is no leakage; it is beyond all merit and achievement. It involves the interplay of the correct and the biased, and is sovereign in every respect.
Yuanwu said: "In these times, if you brothers who engage in inquiry can exhaustively reach the point where the breath is cut off, that is already difficult to attain.

Yet there is still the fact that 'ten thousand existences are not its achievement' remaining. Even if you manage to reach the state where 'ten thousand existences are not its achievement,' there is still..."
It encompasses all existence. Even if one were to reach the point where all existence is encompassed, what can be done against the Dragon King brandishing his sword?
In the teaching of Baoen, it is not so; if one investigates and questions skillfully, there is a principle that leaves no breath to draw.
When one reaches the point where breath ceases, there is the principle of encompassing all phenomena.

When one reaches the point of encompassing all phenomena, there is the principle that all phenomena are not its foundation. *Hè!* Even if you were able to plant and cultivate them, they would not be a forest of pillars and beams.
A monk asked Caoshan, "Who is it within the realm that brandishes his sword? Caoshan said, "Caoshan. The monk said, "Whom do you intend to kill?
Caoshan said, "Not only all others—I kill them all. The monk said, "What if you encounter your own father and mother?
Caoshan said, "Why choose between them? The monk said, "What about yourself? Caoshan said, "Who can do anything to me?"
The monk asked, "Why do you not kill yourself? Caoshan replied, "It is simply that there is no place to begin.

Fuguo commented, "To investigate the beginning and the end, to recognize the appropriate occasion, to distinguish fine nuances, and to skillfully employ indirect methods—Caoshan was certainly not lacking in these qualities;
yet, in the end, he could not avoid 'entering the mud and entering the water. At that time, [Fuguo] should have waited for him to say, 'Why do you not kill yourself?'"
"Give him his proper fodder; what more need be said of having no place to begin? He then took up his staff and said:
"Forged from the light of the seven stars, brilliantly radiant; once mastered, one may roam freely across the world."
Zhengjue said: "Who is it that brandishes the sword? It is a single body, not two separate entities. There is no place for a hand to descend; the direct path admits no private interests.
If one discusses the biased and the correct, the inverted and the deviant, the task is complete. Yet, if one wishes to maintain integrity from beginning to end, there still remains one missing pivot.
Those with the eye of discernment, try to examine this!"

Fohaiyun said: "Caoshan held his sword but did not use it; this was the very style of his school. It is a matter of winding and turning, of mutual interplay, where the end is as good as the beginning.
One must simply ask him: 'At the moment you intend to kill someone, right there, I shall cut you into two pieces.'"
To avoid teaching people how to enter the mud and wade through the water, he still lacked one pivotal turn of phrase.
A monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when the four mountains press in from all sides? Caoshan said, "Caoshan is right inside them.
The monk asked, "I wonder, does he still seek to exit or not? Caoshan said, "Being right inside them, he seeks to exit."
Foguo picked up the case and said: "To grant passage equally is not without the expedient means of a patriarch extending his hand;
yet, alas, it still lacks the skill of holding fast. If it were Jiangshan, and someone were to ask, 'What is it like when the four mountains press in?
I would simply reply, 'It encompasses all existence. Waiting for him to say, 'I wonder if there is still a way out?'"
[The Master] said, "None. [The monk] replied, "The eye of truth is opened at the crown of the head.
Zhengjue said, "The school style of Caoshan involves entering and exiting, shifting and exchanging; it is indeed extraordinary.
If one examines it closely, do not say that the former words do not match the latter."
Fohaiyun said: "Wenyuan said: 'In one sense, this is letting go; it is not that there is no skillful means (upāya) of extending a hand from within the bubble.
Yet, how can one avoid lacking the effort to hold fast? When asked, 'What is it like when the four mountains press in?
he simply replied: 'It encompasses all existence. One must wonder: does it still seek to emerge? The true eye opens at the crown of the head—Caoshan."
Letting go; Yuanwu holds fast. Tianning also enters a portion of it. When the four mountains press in from all sides, what then?
Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, is there still any seeking for an exit? Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru.
A monk asked Caoshan, "What is the true nature of illusion? Caoshan said, "The very essence of illusion is fundamentally true. The monk asked, "When one is in the midst of illusion, what is revealed?
Caoshan said, "In the midst of illusion, it is precisely that which is revealed. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is identical to illusory transformation. Caoshan said: [It is so.]
Having realized that illusions and transformations are unattainable, the Buddha-fruit was held up by [Zhaozhou] and said:
"A half-inch sharp blade cuts through at every point; a single bright lamp destroys darkness as soon as it appears.
Caoshan understood how to break through the den within the den, and thus he saw that in every instance there is a way to emerge.
At this very moment, how shall one tread the path to reach that state of pure emptiness and secure stability,
where when acting, no effort whatsoever is required?
Zhengjue Yun said: "This monk came with a question; Cao Shan replied with an answer. 'Filial piety requires little effort,' and Cao Shan responded, 'A staff strikes the head of a stone man.
Fohai said: 'This is like riding a thief’s horse to seize the thief’s spear. Cao Shan is truly extraordinary; he does not waste a single ounce of strength."
A mere fraction of effort: the gates on both sides open toward the center.
A monk asked Caoshan, "What is the formless site of enlightenment? Caoshan said, "Caoshan’s belly is not large."
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "To build a leaky shelter within empty space is nonetheless a way of encompassing all.
If it were Jiangshan, it would not be so. Suppose someone were to ask, 'What is the formless site of enlightenment? He would reply:
'The Cool and Clear Jewel Mountain, with its myriad bodhisattvas.'"
Zhengjue said: "These two venerable elders conversing in such a manner may be called 'following the same path but taking different tracks.
If someone were to ask me, the mountain monk: 'What is the formless Way-place? I would simply reply:
'A lacquer bucket filled with ink; returning at midnight to dye black cloth. My way is the same as theirs, yet my path is different. Li [continued].
Where does the harm lie? Try examining this for a moment. Fogu Hai said:
"To mold it, one cannot mold it; to paint it, one cannot paint it. If you do not realize it at the moment of the opportunity, there are a thousand mountains facing you.
Tsk! Do not try to divine the future by drilling a tortoise or beating a tile."
Gushan raised the question for Xiuxi: "When sound and form are pure and true, what then? Xiuxi said, "Why does the bowl ring? Gushan walked from east to west and stood there.
Xiuxi said, "If you do not act like this, then trouble will arise. Gushan then walked from west to east and stood there.
Xiuxi stepped down from his meditation seat and walked three or five paces; Gushan seized him and said, "Sound and form are pure and true—what then?"
"How is it? Guishan gave him a slap. Yangshan said, "After a hundred years, will there even be someone to serve tea?
Guishan replied, "What would you do with old man Guyang? Yangshan laughed heartily.
Fojian raised the case and laughed heartily, saying, "How very funny! What is there to laugh at?
Before the tower, clever swallows chatter in pairs; atop the grove, coquettish orioles fly in pairs.
Because I was looking at the nonsensical words of the ancients, I have casually gained another couplet of verse."
Zhengjue said, "Let me ask what this verse means: 'Rising early as the fifth watch draws near, there are still travelers on the road at night.
Fohai said, "The two elders met within sound and form; their deportment lies beyond sound and form.
Upon the monk’s starless scale, one is half a pound and the other is eight ounces. If you do not believe this, then take up your staff horizontally."
Zhàng said, "Look, look! Grasp the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not mistake it for the fixed mark on the scale.
He then cited an occasion when Xiāoyáo ascended the hall one day while Lùxī was standing in attendance. Xiāoyáo said, "Every thought clings to objects; every mind is eternally still.
Lùxī said, "Yesterday there was also someone who spoke in this way. Xiāoyáo asked, "What did he say? Lùxī said, "I do not know."
Xiyun said, "Please, Master, speak. Yaorao suddenly struck him across the mouth with his whisk. Xiyun brushed out his sleeves and departed.
Yaorao said, "The assembly, look! Even those who possess the eye upon the crown of their heads cannot discern this."
Fojian took up the case and said: "Though this old monk lacks eyes upon the crown of his head, I can still discern that your very bones are exposed.
Why? Because the venomous snake in the ancient tomb wears horns on its head, and the fierce tiger of the South Mountain has a shaggy, disheveled tail."
The Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment says: "Though every thought-moment clings to objects, every mind is eternally still. One wanders freely, spreading out one's own niche;
yet before even mounting the stage, one is preempted by Lu Xi. Fortunately, there is a fine performance, resulting in a draw where both sides win equally, and all share in the joy.
Nevertheless, if one does not possess the 'eye on the crown of the head' within this state, how can one discern the mind?"
The mind turns toward those of superior capacity.
Foguo Haiyun said: "To possess the eye upon the crown of the head, it is very easy to discern the deer in the western mountains; however, to discern the one who wanders in leisure is difficult.
Why? Because when the fifth watch of the night has passed and dawn breaks, there are still travelers on the road."
Baizhang of Baoci in Fuzhou questioned a monk: "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Wolong. Baizhang asked, "How long have you been there?
The monk said, "I have spent the winter and passed through the summer. Baizhang said, "The Dragon Gate has no guests who stay overnight;
why have you remained there for so long? The monk said, "In the lion’s den, there are no other beasts. Baizhang said, "Then give us a lion’s roar!"
"Look! The monk said, "If I were to let out a lion's roar, there would be no more Master. Ciyun said, "Out of consideration for you as a newcomer, I grant you thirty blows of the staff."
Fojian took up the case and said: "Baoci’s beating of the grass was intended solely to startle the snake. Who knew that beneath the green thicket there was a golden-haired lion crouching?

Master Fohaiyun shifted the modes and changed the tones upon his stringless lute;

Fojian held up his staff and said, "In those days, vegetables were cheap; radishes covered the ground. For a single coin, one could buy one, and whoever got it would eat their fill with contented snorts.

Buddha-Haiyun: Do you wish to see where the National Teacher lands? His face is three inches thick.
[The Master] cited Xiangshan’s question to a monk: "Where have you come from? As the monk was about to open his mouth, Xiangshan struck him across the mouth with a bamboo itch-scratcher.

This makes the bystanders laugh to death.
