Fohai said, "Strike as soon as you hesitate. A master of the school points and one acts; a sharp-witted monk acts upon being pointed at.
It was simply not so. To cite this:
A monk asked Changsha, "When a person of the highest caliber arrives, how do you see them? Changsha said, "Like the hand of a dead man."
The monk asked, "What is the sphere of activity for those of the highest caliber? Changsha said, "Like the eyes of a dead man.
Fojian commented, "Changsha had only the intention to accept the jade; he lacked the resolve to cut through the city walls. Jiangshan is not like this.
When one of the highest caliber arrives, how do you receive them? 'The water rises and the boat rises high. What is it?"
This is the place where those of the highest caliber tread. *Nītābuddha* is great; tell me, how far apart is this from the ancients?
Try to examine it for yourself. Zhengjue said:
"The hands of the dead have their bloodlines flowing through the entire body; the eyes of the dead have their radiance pervading the world. If it were merely...
To interpret this as a single phrase is to fail Longsha; to fall into the second or third [levels of understanding] is for Longsha to fail Fohai.
"The hand of a dead man" turns back and forth in suchness; "the eyes of a dead man" clearly distinguish light and darkness.
Although this is still "making a living behind closed doors," it has not yet reached "opening the gate to welcome guests. Now, if someone asks: "What is an uppermost person?"
Come! How do you see me? Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of my staff. What is the sphere of activity for those of the highest rank?
The true eye opens at the crown of the head.
A monk asked Changsha, "What is the Dharma-preaching of the insentient? Changsha pointed to a pillar to the east and said, "This one."
The monk said, "Who can hear it? The Master pointed to a pillar on the west side and said, "This one can hear it.
The monk asked, "Does the Master hear it as well? The Master said, "If I were to hear it, who would I have to present this story to?"
Fojian held up [the case] and said: "Although Changsha points east and draws west, he is much like one who mistakes a bell for a jar.
Do you wish to understand the ultimate meaning? The monk drawing water returns to the temple beneath the forest; the boatman stands waiting on the sand at the riverhead."
Zhengjue said: "The old man of Changsha was already able to initiate [the teaching], but he could not carry it through to the end.

At that time, had he waited for him to ask, 'Does the Master hear? and then struck him across the ear with a palm, and then asked him, 'Did you hear?'—if he had attained realization then, one would have seen the true hand of the tiger."
Fohaiyun’s "Clouds over the Buddha-ocean" and Changsha’s response to the dialogue differ in two respects; Fojian’s critical commentary, however, treats them as one and the same case.
The case is cited: A monk asked Changsha, "Where has Nanquan gone now that he has passed away?
Changsha said, "When Shitou was a novice śrāmaṇera, he visited the Sixth Patriarch. The monk said, "I am not asking about when Shitou was a novice śrāmaṇera visiting the Sixth Patriarch."
After Nanquan had passed away, a monk asked, "Where has he gone? Sandow said, "I will have him go searching for himself.
The monk said, "I thought the Master had only a thousand-foot cold pine, yet you have no sprouting stone shoot. Sandow did not answer.
The monk said, "Thank you, Master, for your reply," but Sandow still did not answer. The monk reported this to Sansheng, who said, "I have always suspected this fellow."
"Even so, I must wait until I go myself to ask before I can understand. The next day, Sansheng went to inquire:

"Yesterday, when the Master spoke these words to that monk, it was truly brilliant, surpassing all who came before and leaving none behind; it is something rarely heard from ancient times to the present. Yet you did not respond. [Baizhang] replied, "I did not respond."
He asked again, "What is the second moon? The monk said, "It does not truly exist. The Master prostrated himself. The monk then offered this verse: "How wondrous! How wondrous!
Within the reality of one moon, there is doubt regarding two moons. Seeing and the conditions for seeing have no self-nature."
"In quiescent permanence, who is right and who is wrong?
Fojian took up the case and said: "How extraordinary! How extraordinary! Changsha painted a tiger, yet it turned out to be a wildcat.
Once Nanquan departed, there has been no news; he leaves travelers only to engage in talk of right and wrong."
Again, because a monk asked, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing? the Master took up the matter once more and said, "I will give you a parable.
It is like someone asking for the road to Tiantai, yet being pointed toward Nanyue."
When someone asks for the way to Mount Wutai, he instead points them toward Mount Emei. One day, within the city of Chang’an, before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, they shall meet.
Having traversed all at once Mount Zhurong, Stone Bridge, Mañjuśrī, and Samantabhadra, he raises his whisk and says:
"Do you wish to see Mount Zhurong, Stone Bridge, Mañjuśrī, and Samantabhadra? They are all here with this mountain monk."
At the tip of the whisk, those who understand realize that different paths lead to the same destination; those who do not, should refrain from following words to produce intellectual interpretations.
Zhengjue said: "The old man Changsha, arriving at this point, was certainly thorough and subtle; it was much like sifting sand to select gold.
Were it not for an artisan’s eye that is penetratingly clear, one would inevitably sweep away both the gold and the sand together."
Buddha-Haiyun asked about the east but answered about the west; within his words there was resonance, surpassing all that came before and all that followed.

Within these phrases he concealed the blade—do you wish to know where the essential point lies? To further assist you, here is another verse: How wondrous! How truly wondrous! In rolling up and unfolding, appearing and disappearing, observe the total function.
Were it not for the discerning eyes of Zhang Hua, One could not avoid following others in their judgments of right and wrong.
The monk Xiaoyin asked, "When the light of the spirit pierces through heaven and earth, what is the state of affairs within, without, and in between?
Feng said, "Your Reverence has quite good eyes. The monk said, "If it is so difficult to see, it must have been brought out by my teacher as well."
Feng said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice! The patrol station here is not far off. The monk then gave a shout. Feng covered his mouth.
The monk said, "Old Monk, having been given one of my shouts, you are left with eyes staring and mouth agape.
Feng then shouted. The monk covered his ears and went out. Feng said, "This is a treacherous spy!"

The Eye of Heaven and Earth encounters the Eye that examines people, the Eye of study, and the Eye that discerns dharmas. Eye meets eye, shining upon one another, continuous and without leakage."
The clam and the shrimp grapple with one another; yet they fall into the hands of the fisherman. Here, cast a single eye.
Jiangshan grants you the possession of the eye. Do you wish to know? The dragon swallows the moon of a thousand years; within its brain lies the night-bright pearl.

What kind of tally-stick is that which Yongming transmits?

Fojian took up the case and said: "When one reaches the river, the land of Wu ends; beyond the bank, the mountains of Yue abound. Zhengjue said:

It is like joining together echoes and responding to empty sounds.

He led the Great King, the Grand Guardian, and the Duke.

Ultimately, how should one understand it? Generalissimo Great King! Grand Guardian Duke!

This too is a clumsy fellow pulling a dull saw.

A monk asked, "What is it like when the hole is empty? Mount [Shan] said, "You must simply go for ten thousand years. The monk asked, "What is it like after ten thousand years?

Mount [Shan] said, "Let your boots shine; let them shine as you wish. Let them be wrapped up; let them be wrapped up as you wish. He asked again, "What is 'long'? Mount [Shan] said: [He remained silent.]
"A thousand sages cannot measure it. The Monk asked, "What is short? Shanshan said, "It does not even fill the eye of a gnat.
Fuguo commented, "These two venerable elders each hold a living serpent’s pearl and embrace a jade disc from Mount Jing.
When they bring them forth, they are indeed extraordinary. Nevertheless, if someone were to ask Jiangshan about a single hair—"
"How is it when piercing through all the apertures? He replied, "You must simply let your whole body pass through. "After the whole body has passed through, what then?
"Be desolate as you wish; be carefree as you wish. "What is long? "Planting a staff until it becomes a forest—the matter is already manifest.
"What is short? "Even using a peck to measure side by side, it still falls short by half. "Do you all understand?"
Ma! This is a distinct school of springtime. Zhengjue said:
"If someone asks, 'What is it like when a single hair pierces through all the holes? simply say, 'You must meet it directly. After meeting it directly, what then?
Let the provisional city (the *pūrva-nimitta*) be your provisional city; let the treasure land (the *ratnasthāna*) be your treasure land."
"What is long? "A single ray of white hair-light between the eyebrows. "What is short? "The great scripture that does not move amidst the dust.
Do you understand? Three people have taken a tortoise and turned it into a turtle.
Buddha-Sea Cloud: Those who tread the path of truth and reality find that the phrase "the same wind blowing across a thousand li" fits like a tally and its seal.
Yet, one cannot avoid following along with even a single fraction; it is not merely a matter of copying a pattern.
Furthermore, regarding the time when a single hair pierces through many holes—how is this? You must attain resonance. Once resonance is attained, how is it? Eradicate it.
Let you uproot and eliminate as you wish; let you establish as you wish. What is long? The fragrant blossoms of the spring orchid and autumn rhododendron possess a subtle scent.
What is short? Do not concern yourself with any right or wrong at all.
To cite the case of Master Dadian of Chaozhou: A monk came to visit him. As soon as Dadian saw him, he held up his itch-comb.

The monk looked at it with his eyes. Dadian said, "When you go to other places, do not say that you have visited Dadian. The monk said: [The text here implies the monk's subsequent departure or silence].
The monk borrowed Master Danyuan’s itchy patch (a skin ailment). When he brought it up for discussion among various quarters, Danyuan said, "If you see my itchy patch, feel free to bring it up.
The monk brushed his sleeves and departed. Danyuan said, "Had I known it would be so, I would not have seen it as such."
Foguo held up his staff and said: "This monk is like one who carves sores into healthy flesh. When Mazu Daian died, he did not even offer condolences.
At that time, had I waited for him to borrow a 'itching-and-soothing' phrase, I would have struck him a blow right through the chest to prevent him from taking error for truth.
Do you all understand? Real brass does not trade for gold."
Zhengjue said, "Dadian said, 'Had I known it would be like this earlier, I would not have seen it as such. Does he approve of this monk, or does he not?
Do you wish to understand? A thousand times looking with the eyes is not as good as one time scooping with the hands."
Fohaiyun held up his itch-scratcher. The monk looked at it; [Fohaiyun] entered directly with a single blade.
"If you travel to various quarters, do not say that it is good to have visited Dadian. Half-closed, half-open, borrow the Master’s itch-scratcher and show it to those in the various quarters.
Whether both are bright or both are dark, if you see the itch-scratcher, feel free to show it to them."
"Why do you not cut it off for him at once? The monk brushed out his sleeves and went out. "A true practitioner! A true practitioner! [The Master said:
"Had I known it would be thus, I would not have seen it as such. He is well-versed in employing this device. He then called to the assembly, saying, "Do you know where Dayuan fell?"
Baizhang Sanping raised the question of Dayuan: "Do not point east and scratch west; I ask the Master to point directly.
Dayuan said, "A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou. Sanping said, "That is still pointing east and scratching west. Dayuan said, "If you were a phoenix chick..."
"Do not seek it over there. [The monk] prostrated flatly. Duan said, "If you do not grasp the latter phrase, the former discourse will be difficult to complete.
Foguo commented, "This is the thoroughgoing, compassionate heart of a grandmother; one does not seek it over there. Father and son must meet in mutual resonance."
"Entering the weeds for no reason.
Zhengjue said, "Even if Dadian speaks in such a manner, he has still not fully resolved the previous statement. Why?
The public case is right here before us."

Buddha-Haiyun said: "The karmic conditions for raising a child cannot avoid falling into the weeds. As for Sanping’s initial insults followed by later reverence, let us set aside his willingness to endure such obscurity for now.
But as for the stone man squatting at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou—how is it ultimately?
If you so much as touch him, he will break your donkey’s back."
Master Shuikong went to visit Dadian. Dadian seized his sitting mat and said, "There is no need to exchange greetings of the season, nor is there any need to state where you have come from.
Shuikong said, "I was about to ask such a question, yet I feared it would be insufficient as a matter of human courtesy.
Dadian let go of the mat and said, "Is it now sufficient? Shuikong lifted up the sitting mat and said, "If I were to exchange greetings of the season, I fear it would lead to further delusion."
Regarding the place of origin, Dadian said, "It does not matter even if we meet for a brief moment.
Foguo commented: "Dadian was skilled at both holding fast and letting go; Shuikong was able to support the beginning and join the end.
It was like gold and jade resonating together, like lightning striking and stars flying; it was like glue being poured onto glue, or lacquer being joined with lacquer. Even so..."

If one does not understand the timing of the season, one fears losing the way back to where one came from. If one intends to proceed in this manner, yet fears that human sentiments may be insufficient—precisely at such a moment, how should one act?
Where the bamboo is dense, it does not hinder the flowing stream from passing through; though the heavens are high, they do not obstruct the white clouds from flying.
Zhengjue said, "O Wise One! The two peaches and three men have attained equal division.
Fohai said, "The Great Head whirled it out and whirled it back in; water and sky seem both intended and unintended. Their words and spirit were in harmony.
When human sentiments are fully satisfied, everyone inevitably becomes deluded regarding their place of origin.
To cite the Venerable Qinghua of Yuezhou: a monk asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? Qinghua replied:
The Yangtze River flows without interruption; gathered foam drifts at the mercy of the wind. A monk asked, "Does it still receive sacrificial offerings?
Huizhao said, "Sacrificial offerings are certainly not lacking. The monk asked, "What are the sacrificial offerings? Huizhao said, "Fishermen’s songs and the beating of oars;
the sound is heard within the valley."

Foguo picked it up and said: "To clarify the potential by borrowing from phenomena, to sing forth from within nothingness—this is because the patch-robed monk has the talisman beneath his elbows and arms, and possesses the eye upon the crown of his head.
Thus, he acts as master wherever he is and takes the occasion as his school.
Even so, he is still within the nest. Suppose someone were to ask Jiangshan: 'When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?'"
"Where have you gone? He replied to him: "The ten-thousand-year-old void has never moved; does it still receive offerings?
"It certainly does. "What are these offerings? "Day after day, incense and flowers; night after night, lamps."
Zhengjue said: "If you ask this mountain monk, 'Where does a deceased monk go when he passes away?
I would simply reply: 'The green mountains have no front or back. What is the offering? The warbling birds know the spring for themselves."
Fohaiyun: Although Qinghua’s words and meaning are intimate and direct, they only reach eighty percent.
Someone asked Nengren, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? [Nengren replied,] "Neither south of the Yangtze nor north of it.
What is the offering? The profound meaning of pure tea can also intoxicate people. If you can offer this here, I grant that you have emerged from the darkness.
Jie (Jiexian) cites Master Shao Shan of Luoyang. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Shao Shan? Shao Shan said, "Ancient and modern monkeys and birds cry out;
emerald hues are shrouded in thin mist. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? Shao Shan said, "Step back."
"Clouds of the Buddha-ocean," [Foyan] said. "You should simply pay him one prostration. Foguo took up the point and said:
"It is like a skilled archer whose every arrow hits the mark. Were it not for this state, one would not be worthy of being called such a person;
were it not for such a person, they would not be fit to dwell in this state. This is what is meant by 'the ancients and the present'—without interval and without interruption."
Do you understand? Shaoshan is still here. Zhengjue said:
"If asked about the realm of Shaoshan, answer: 'It cannot be painted; it cannot be sketched.
What is it like for one within that realm? Step back! You have hit your own mouth."
Buddha-Sea Cloud: The realm of Mount Shao is most excellent; mist enshrouds its light green hues. One wishes to paint it, yet cannot finish;
the cries of monkeys and birds resound one after another.
A monk asked Master Shao, "What is the nature of all phenomena? Shao replied, "A bird flies through the white void of the sky; the mountain is far away."
The color was a deep blue. The monk said, "If that is so, then all characteristics are gone. Xishan said, "I knew well in advance that you would misunderstand in a confused way.
Fuguo picked up the case and said, "Since it is not permitted to understand it in such a way, then how else should one understand it? Do you truly comprehend this?"
Ma! Turning iron into gold is not difficult.
Zhengjue said: "The old man of Shaoshan made it difficult first and easy later.
Fohai said: "When asked in this way and answered in this way, why is it that he does not permit understanding it in this way?"
There was a monk named Yuzun Bunan who came to visit Shao Shan. Upon reaching the foot of the mountain, he saw Shao Shan and asked, "Where does the road to Shao Shan lead?
Shao Shan pointed with his finger and said, "It goes toward where the Wuna Forest is dark green.
Yuzun stepped forward, seized him, and said, "I have long heard of Shao Shan; is it truly so? Shao Shan replied, "It is indeed so, but you, O Acharya..."
"What is it? Zhen asked. "I intend to pose a question," he continued. "Will you answer me, Master? Shan said, "I suspect you are not made of 'golden teeth' (a master craftsman);
how else could you bend the bow to shoot Wei Chi? Zhen said, "The phoenix soars directly into the misty heights; who fears the wild sparrows in the woods?
Shan said, "The great drum hangs before the hall for you to strike as you please; try then to display your family style like an elder."
The monk Zun said, "A single phrase transcends the thousand sages; the pine and the vine do not equal the lunar disc.
Shan said, "Even if you were to emerge directly beyond the time of Wei-yin, you would still be half a month's journey behind Shao-shan. Zun asked, "I wonder where the fault lies?
Shan said, "Such bold words are known only by people of the present age. Zun said, "If that is so, then true jade is [hidden] in the mud."
Zhongyi did not dismiss the myriad activities of the sensory world. Shanshan said, "Under the school of Lu Ban, they merely display their cleverness and ingenuity.
Zhenzun said, "I am just like this; how about you, Master? Shanshan said, "The jade maiden throws her shuttle at night, weaving brocade in the western house.
Zhenzun said, "Is this not your own family style, Master? Shanshan said, "The plowman fashions the jade water-clock. It does not [end there].
This was done by a practitioner of the Way. Zun asked, "This is still merely literary expression. What is the true style of the Master’s house?
Shanshan said, "Lying across the body to face the universe—who is there to show their head? He added, "The *śrāmaṇera* possesses the spirit that pierces the heavens."

The old monk has a wedge that drives into the ground; you, O Acharya, attempt to swallow the vast ocean whole. The old monk carries Mount Sumeru on his back; you, O Acharya, come forward with sword drawn.
The old monk stands waiting with spear leveled; speak quickly, speak quickly! Regarding the single path leading upward—speak! Zun said, "A bright mirror stands upon its stand;
I pray the Master will examine it. Shan said, "I do not examine it. Zun asked, "Why do you not examine it?"
"In shallow water there are no fish; it is but a laborious effort to cast down the hook. Cizun said nothing. Shanshan struck him. Foguo took up the case, saying:
"Cizun the patch-robed monk was like a tiger with its horns—majestic and full of awe-inspiring power.
Yet how could he avoid Shaoshan knowing how to seize the tiger’s head and gather in its tail? Thus he was able to ascend higher step by step, with every sound in perfect resonance. Do you know?"
As for the resting place of these two elders: "A master among masters boasts of his mastery; a red heart shoots at a red heart.

Zhengjue said: "Adapting to the times and responding to changes, following things through their success and failure—whose can distinguish the male from the female in the aspirations of the wild geese?"
The Marquis of Han had not yet met his match; his family tradition was one of coarse cotton robes. That he rolled up the Three Qin like a mat was no mere whim;

why labor to recall Kuai Tong’s arguments on loyalty and righteousness? Foghai said: "In the Battle of Kunyang of the Han dynasty, dragons and snakes vied for victory, while tigers and leopards lost their majesty. To compare this with...
As for Master Zun of Shaoshan, he was more than ten thousand miles away like white clouds. When Master Zun remained silent, you must by no means understand this silence as mere speechlessness.
Why? Because it is known with certainty that one who discerns the conditions of advancing or retreating, and of existing or perishing, is from beginning to end nothing other than a true master.

Pufu raised his whisk. The monk said, "If so, today I have encountered an enlightened ruler.
Pufu said, "It is like a melody that is barely fit to be heard, yet is blown by the wind into another tune."
Foguo held up his whisk and said, "To verify a person at the point of ultimate certainty, one must know the sound the moment they open their mouth.
Zhengjue said, "If it were not for being blown by the wind into a different tune, such a melody would be difficult to withstand."
Buddha-Sea Cloud: "If one does not examine forms and listen to sounds, it will be a disaster, a disaster!
A monk asked Luopu, "At a precipice ten thousand fathoms high, one must advance further; how can one avoid losing one's life? Luopu said, "Mount Sumeru is tied with a lotus fiber.
The monk asked, "What kind of realm is this? Luopu said, "An upturned lotus atop the flagpole."
The monk said, "It is profoundly still and utterly clear. Pufu said, "One must turn the body once more atop the summit of Mount Sumeru.
The monk said, "In that case, one must remain cautious and earnest. Pufu said, "Vainly following a decoy pigeon, you lose your life within the net.
The monk asked, "How can one avoid being led away? Pufu said, "The neck of the parrot-bottle is small; though it seeks to soar toward heaven, it cannot pass through."
Foguo held up his staff and said: "Luopu exerted the skillful means of a master; he untied what was stuck and removed what was bound, until he had exhausted every hammer and tongs.
This monk was full of apprehension and trepidation; in the end, the world of black and yellow dazzled his eyes, and he could not help but follow it upward and downward.
If one were truly a person of great liberation, cutting through everything in two strokes with a single blow—what difficulty would there be? Do you understand?"
Simma: "At a ten-thousand-fathom high peak, one can let go; throughout boundless lands, one may roam at will.
Zhengjue said: "This monk’s gate of death is difficult to face; it draws forth Luopu’s life as if hanging by a thread.
Although Foguo understands letting go and roaming, this too is merely a forced livelihood. (Sighs)"
Fohaiyun said: "This monk has spent so much effort on Luopo;
though his state may be profound and serene, and his resolve earnest and urgent, he is still a full step short of the ten-thousand-fathom precipice. But where exactly does his error lie?"
A monk asked Luopu: "The two kings are present at the banquet; dragon and snake have not yet been distinguished. In this struggle to save the world from calamity, who has the most urgent heart?
Luopu said: "He who tramples through the Hongmen Pass. The monk said: "Who knows that from ancient times to the present, one remains unaware as they fall into the void? Luopu said: [Silence].
"Greedy only for fragrant bait, his body remains stuck in the snare. The monk said, "Even if the Master’s ancient mirror were hung at the doorway, it would still be beset by wild fox spirits.
Pufeng said, "Today this mountain monk has fought a great battle in vain. The monk let out a tiger's roar, and Pufeng struck him with a staff.
The monk collapsed as soon as he was struck by the staff. Baopu said, "What limit is there for those who die under the blow of the staff? The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed.
Baopu said, "A hunting dog does not die beneath the bed."
Foguo held up his staff and said: "This monk raises with one hand and presses down with the other. Yet Lo Pu was able to seize the tiger’s head and gather its tail;
it could be said that he was a thief who recognized a thief, a connoisseur who recognized a connoisseur.

Nevertheless, though this was so, they were unaware and unknowing, turning the conversation into two separate pieces. I dare ask: where is the place where the conversation is split into two? If you wish to recognize it—"
"True gold is seen within the fire.
Zhengjue said, "This monk is a fox feigning the majesty of a tiger; he has been defeated by the hands of benevolence and righteousness.
Fohai said, "In front he hides his body while revealing his shadow; behind he bares his mouth and shows his fangs. Had it not been for the ancient mirror..."
Facing the carriage window, one cannot avoid being a wild fox spirit.
A monk asked Luopu, "The Dharma-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any categories; is this so? Luopu said, "It would be better to cherish your eyebrows.
The monk asked, "How can one avoid this fault? Luopu said, "A clay tortoise may live for a thousand years, but in the end it will never..."

Jie followed [the master] like a crane among the clouds. The monk said, "Even you, Sun Bin, shall suffer humiliation and emasculation. Pufu said, "A noseless ox—what place is there for it to be driven?
The monk then threw himself to the ground and bellowed like an ox. Pufu said, "This beast! The monk then gave a shout.
Puyuan said, "Hiding his tail while showing his teeth—he is certainly no adept.
Foguo took up the case and said, "This monk seems to see and yet does not see; he seems to understand and yet does not understand.
Were it not for a precious mirror set upon its stand, how could one verify that he has lost his trace and forfeited his substance? Tell me, is there still a flaw right now?"
[Zhaozhou said: "There is none. In the autumn of the eighth month, where is there heat?
Zhengjue said: "If that monk had been present at that time, he would have said: 'The Master's nostrils are perfectly intact;
what need is there for anything to ward it off?'"
Buddha-Haiyun: This monk raised his head five times, and Luopu suppressed him five times. Where, then, lies the point of contention?
Hiding the tail while baring the teeth—boasting of being a skilled hand. In the public hall, not even a single speck of partiality is tolerated.
A monk asked Luopu: "There is no question and no answer; I ask the Master to provide a response. Luopu said, "You are not Ding Yao.
The monk said, "Thank you, Master, for your response. Luopu said, "Nine in the middle, seven at the bottom."
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "The rat was caught, but the oil jar was broken; small kindness obstructs great kindness.
Why not give him fodder appropriate to his own station?
Zhengjue said: "This monk’s flowery words are incomplete; Luopo’s Sanskrit characters are written horizontally."
Buddha’s ocean-clouds: the waters of Luopo are vast and boundless, a myriad *qīng* deep and unfathomable.
This monk takes a single scoop with a broken ceramic bowl and causes it to dry up to its very bottom. How truly laughable!
Nevertheless, congratulations to the General for achieving a complete victory; those who return are no fewer than those who departed.
Citing Master Yunju of Mount Lu: A monk asked, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas?
Yunju immediately shouted, saying, "You little farmer! The monk bowed, and Yunju asked, "How do you understand this? The monk shouted, "This old monk!"
Jiuyun said, "It turns out you do not understand. The monk performed a dance and departed. Jiuyun said, "A beggar following the food tray.
Fuguo commented, "Recognizing the opportune moment and distinguishing between fortune and misfortune requires an eye capable of mutual resonance and turning the pivot.
Among a thousand or ten hundred people, it is difficult to find even one or half of one. Why, then, did he end up as a beggar following the food tray? It was also thus."
"Out of pity for his son, he does not perceive his ugliness.
Zhengjue said, "Although they are both of one kind—beggarly—they know how to follow along the bottom of the tray; they are indeed worthy of reward.
Fohai said, "The old fellow Yunju has slightly revealed half his face. This rustic fellow from the fields sees it as soon as he sees it."
To shatter the Great Tang Empire and find someone who can even handle the bottom of a tray is difficult indeed.
A monk asked Yunju, "What is the one dharma? Yunju said, "What are the various dharmas? The monk said, "I do not yet understand how to comprehend this.
Yunju said, "The one dharma is your original mind; the various dharmas are your original nature. And so it is.
Dao: Are mind and nature one or two? The monks prostrated. Jū then offered this verse: The One Dharma is the source of all dharmas;
The myriad dharmas are penetrated by the single mind. It is mind alone, it is your very nature; I speak of neither difference nor sameness.
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "For a long time I have heard that Yunju Hongjue is the legitimate son of Dongshan;
I thought he would employ the full 'nose-ring' of a true monk, but it turns out that even when he speaks of 'sometimes,' he is merely dragging through mud and wading through water.
According to my own view at Jiangshan, what could one call 'mind-nature, one or two'? To add more mud on top of dirt is yet another layer."
Zhengjue said, "The Buddha-fruit is like this; one only knows the first part and does not know the second.
Fohai said, "The boundless wholesome causes from the preceding discourse and praise."
One day Yunju ascended the hall and said: "It is like a man who spends thirty strings of cash to buy a hunting dog;
it only knows how to track those that leave footprints or a scent. But when it encounters a wild sheep hanging from a horn, let alone footprints—"
There was not even a breath of air. The monk then asked, "What is it like when the wild goat has not yet hung its horns?
Ju replied, "Six times six is thirty-six. The monk asked, "What is it like after the horns have been hung? Ju replied, "Six times six is thirty-six. The monk bowed. Ju asked, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. Ju said, "Have you not heard it said: 'All traces are cut off'? Fuguo added a comment.
The monk said, "When the fish swims, the water becomes turbid. He reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "Master Yunju is still alive.
The monk then asked, "What is it like when the antelope has not yet hung its horns? Zhaozhou said, "Nine times nine is eighty-one. The monk said, "It is truly as difficult to understand as that.
Zhaozhou said, "What is so difficult to understand? The monk said, "Please explain it to me, Master. Zhaozhou said, "New..."
Regarding "La Xīnláo," Fuguo added a comment, saying: "The fish swims and the water is turbid. A monk again asked Changqing, "How is it when the antelope has not yet hung its horns?
Changqing said, "A fellow among the grass. The monk asked, "How is it after the horns have been hung? Changqing said, "He is crying out in confusion. The monk asked, "What is it ultimately?
Changqing said, "The donkey’s business has not yet departed, and the horse’s business has already arrived. Fuguo [added his comment].
He remarked: "When the fish swims, the water becomes turbid.

Fuguo further picked up the point and said: "If we discuss these three venerable masters, one among them attained the essence, one attained the function, and one possessed both essence and function together. If you can verify this and discern it clearly, do not..."
Speaking of the "Way as a Monkey": whether the horn is hung or not hung, one reaches a point where there is simply no place to escape.
Even for this mountain monk to speak in such a manner is like "the fish moving and the water becoming turbid."
Zhengjue said: "The antelope hangs its horns from a tree; one covers one's nose while stealing fragrance; when fish swim, the water becomes turbid;
a domestic thief is difficult to guard against. Fohai said: "Yunju and Zhaozhou have both been convicted of the same offense; only Changqing has a slight advantage."
Master Tong’an Pipai was reading a scripture when a monk came to visit him. Pipai covered his head with the sleeves of his robe.
The monk stepped forward and made a gesture of condolence. Pipai lowered his sleeves and held up the scripture, asking, “Do you understand?
The monk then covered his own head with his sleeves. Pipai cried out, “Heaven! Heaven!”
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "Coming and going face-to-face, guest and host interchange roles.
All are alike in playing with the eyes of a ghost; among them, this is truly strange. This is what is called the samādhi of the playful exercise of supernormal powers.
Nevertheless, how can it compare to treading on solid ground? But what is the place where one treads on solid ground? Blue sky and bright day."
Zhengjue said, "Tongan, 'Recalling the power of Avalokiteśvara'—this monk must return it to the person himself.
Fohai said, "In one sense, this is a matter of mutual exchange; yet, alas, the guest is able to die but unable to live."
A monk asked Master Tong’an Pi, “What is the house style of your monastery? Pi said, “The golden rooster carries its chicks back to the Milky Way;
the jade hare conceives her fetus and enters the Purple Microcosm. The monk said, “If a guest suddenly arrives, how will you receive them?
Pi said, “The golden fruit was plucked by a monkey at dawn; the jade flower was carried back by a phoenix at dusk.”
Foguo held up [the whisk] and said: "Its loftiness is indeed unimpeded; its elegance is truly elegant.

Regarding the five ranks of partiality and correctness, and the sovereign and subject—within these words, they are perfectly appropriate. Nevertheless, in the lineage of Caodong, one outshines the past and leaves nothing behind.
As for the style of the Linji school, how could it tolerate any compromise? If someone were to ask Jiangshan, 'What is...'"
The ancestral style of our Master: when faced with him, one’s very gallbladder is exposed upon opening one's mouth. Yet, when a guest suddenly arrives, how does one attend to them?
It is like leaping through the Diamond Circle and swallowing the Thorny Tamarisk Fruit.
Zhengjue said: "The letter on the silk is like lingering snow; it has been fashioned into a pair of carp. If you wish to know what is in my heart, look at the writing within my belly.

Fohai said: "His family style is noble and wealthy; his countenance is majestic and dignified. Naturally, the cadence of his speech is profound and mysterious, embodying both the orthodox and the deviant."
Zizai (Master Zizai) then raised his staff and said, "Tell me, how far is this from that? He struck the ground once.
He then cited Master Tong’an Cha, who, while gazing at the moon, said, "How marvelous! The stars are bright and the moon is clear; it is truly fit for contemplation—is this not the Way?
A monk asked, "What is the Way? Cha said, "Try telling me what it is. The monk said, "That [moon] of itself..."
"No wound. Do not injure it. Chaya said, "He carries his book-satchel to study literature; he has no leisure for bow and arrow.
Foguo held up his staff and said, "If one can penetrate through and act with swift utility, not injuring the tip and not offending the hand—this monk indeed knows shame.
Why did he say, 'He has no leisure for bow and arrow'? It is precisely because he is so extremely clear that he, conversely, causes..."
The attainment was slow.
Zhengjue said, "Under the gate of Tong’an, if one did not indulge in lofty chanting and hearty feasting, how could one appreciate such pure joy?
Although this monk’s deportment is admirable, alas, he cannot withstand such grand ceremony."
Buddha-Haiyun: "A fine day and a beautiful scene; a pleasing mind and a joyful occasion—these four things are all present together.

This monk has been able to partake in pure delight and witness this magnificent ceremony. At that time, [the Master] said, "Try and say something," whereupon the monk replied, "The stars are bright and the moon is clear;
it is truly worthy of contemplation. One can take for granted that a harmonious atmosphere will pervade."
Master Chacha of Tongan was asked by a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jiangxi.
Chacha said, "How does the Dharma-way of Jiangxi differ from that here? The monk said, "Fortunately, I have encountered someone who asks me this; had I met anyone else..."
"Calamity has arisen. Yuanzhe said, "The old monk was just a moment too hasty. The monk said, "I am no infant;
I shall not merely weep over yellow leaves. Yuanzhe said, "To spare the turtle while harming the tortoise—killing or giving life depends on me."

Foguo held up his staff and said: "In the house of a patriarch, one wields the tongs and hammer of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; when the principle is reached, action must follow immediately, leaving no trace behind.
Since this monk has already come to every door and threshold, what more need be said? To spare the tortoise while injuring the turtle—why strike him across the back with the staff?
For what reason? Under a heavy reward, there will surely be brave men."
Zhengjue said, "Tongan was as usual; he had his head grabbed and his feet pinched by others. Today, I observe that he is in a state beyond doubt.
Although he possesses the freedom to kill or give life, alas, the sword has already been lost."
Fohaiyun said: "What common ground for conversation does this monk have?
To casually ask a question and immediately emit a stench like excrement that permeates others—well, he deserves a severe beating! Why? Because merit must be rewarded."
A monk asked Master Cha, "You have long cultivated the profound and subtle; how do you thoroughly understand it? Cha said, "This old monk is hard of hearing; ask with a loud voice.
The monk said, "A swift hawk does not strike at a sparrow by the fence. Cha said, "One who looks into a mirror in the dark—who can distinguish beauty from ugliness?
The monk said, "How do you thoroughly understand the supreme mechanism? Cha said, "Why bother? The monk said, "Stop."
Xiu said, "He began by boarding the boat, intending to cross the Jian River.
Foguo picked up the thread and said, "Tongan’s head was a dragon, but his tail was a snake; this monk likewise withdrew from the path midway.
If one examines them closely, neither has reached completion. But how can they be brought to a definitive end? One must kill them!"
"One must see blood; when acting for others, one must act with thoroughness. Zhengjue said:
"In the same furnace, cold and heat change according to the season. This monk probes the hot water, then extends his hand and immediately withdraws it.
Fohai said: "The gate having been opened, it is closed again; the soldiers were about to attack, yet they desist once more. This is no mere ruse."
Nor is it out of timidity; it is simply because we are both guests from Jiangnan that one does not wish to sing the *zhègū* (partridge) song too often.

A monk asked Master Chá: "I, your student, do not yet understand the timing of the occasion; I pray the Master will give me instruction. Chá said: "The pines and bamboos are uneven, as thin mists coalesce;
the peaks and ridges are layered, as the moon rises late. The monk was about to offer further words when Chá said: "Armor and weapons!"

Before he had even given [the robe], the thief’s true nature was already revealed. The monk asked, "What do you think of this? Guo Cha replied: "Vital Yang-energy is not trimmed like bamboo before the frost;
ink and water vainly boast of the dragon of the sea. The monk circled the meditation seat once, laughed loudly, and departed.
Guo Cha said, "Closing one's eyes to eat a snail—what a bitter and sour ordeal!"
Foguo held up the staff and said, "To use many to suppress the few, and to use the strong to overpower the weak—is this not easy in principle?
Yet one must still guard against the fact that even in soft mud there may be thorns. Tong'an presented his case in a single stroke; this monk possessed a full measure of refined style.

But how could he compare to the peace and harmony found right where one is? Suppose someone were to ask Jangshan: "The student does not yet understand the timing of the occasion; I beg for instruction."
The Master pointed this out, saying to him: "When entering a temple, look at its nameplate; when entering a village, ask about its customs.
At mealtime there is rice; at dawn there is congee. Zhengjue said:
"Tongan only knew how to shift and exchange according to the occasion, but was unaware that his true eye had gone astray. At that time—
Relying on this monk, he laughed heartily and left it at that; he managed to maintain his composure for a moment, yet was easily toppled by him.
Look—who will suffer the bitterness?
Fohaiyun said: "When this monk asked in such a manner, his identity as a thief was already revealed. When Tongan answered in such a manner, his armor had not yet been donned.
At that moment, when the monk was about to offer a further word, he simply prostrated himself. This is like closing one's eyes while eating a snail;
it was only when Tongan took charge of the matter himself that he finally succeeded."
Jucha asked a monk, "When good and evil are not contemplated, the essence of mind manifests of itself. Does this accord with the principle of the ancients, or not?
The monk said, "Is this not precisely the profound intent of the ancients? Jucha said, "A foreigner drinking milk, yet instead blaming the skilled physician.
The monk bowed and departed. Jucha said, "If you go to other places, do not say that you have come to see Tongan."
Foguo held up [the whisk] and said: "The fragrant bait on the hook—its intent lies in the magnificent fish.
As soon as it is pulled, it turns its body and slips away. Fortunately, Tongan possessed the necessary skill. Do you all know the final phrase?
'Not offending the clear waves, the meaning is naturally distinct.'"

Zhengjue said, "This monk’s single response was perfectly consistent with principle; yet although Tong’an established his gate and walls deeply, he could not help but expose his own family’s disgrace."

In the Ocean-Cloud of the Buddha, when the leader chants once, the harmonizers respond accordingly; their melodies and rhythms are so perfectly attuned that they cannot fail to delight the ears of the assembly.
Although they may shift scales and change keys, they invariably preserve the harmony of the spirit.

is it divided or undivided? A monk said, "Undivided. Jucha said, "Had it not been for you, Dharma brother, this old monk would not have understood."

One day, while Master Jucha was touring the mountains followed by the assembly, he said, "The emerald bamboos before the steps, the yellow chrysanthemums beneath the pavilion—ancient worthies called these 'True Suchness' and 'Prajñā.
Tongan, however, would not have it so. A monk said, "The ancients were also excellent, Master.
Jucha replied, "Not coveting the taste of fragrant bait; one may truly be called a dragon in the azure abyss. The monk said, "The eyes of all quarters [are upon you]."
Muzhe asked, "I do not find it strange that Tao Qian closed his eyes during the Mid-Autumn festival and sat there, yet laughed at the moon for lacking light.
Chacha said, "The green bamboos before the steps and the yellow chrysanthemums beneath the terrace—what of them? The monk said, "Annan has not yet submitted;
how could Sebei have surrendered? The monk bowed. Chacha said, "His fame is heard everywhere."
Foguo commented: "The foundation is firm and solid; the vital pulse flows through without obstruction. Tong’an was skilled at seizing and releasing, rolling up and unrolling.
This monk understood how to snatch the flag and seize the drum. It is what is called a golden chain of linked rings, continuing on without interruption.
To know the matter as it truly is, one must ask those who dwell within it."
Zhengjue said: "At the place where Tong'an went mountain-walking, one might say he was strolling with measured steps and chanting aloud.
This monk followed along, walking slowly as if about to rest; it was truly elegant and refined. It is just as Foguo said: 'Like golden chains linked together.'"
The succession continues without interruption. To know the fundamental matter, one must question those who dwell within it; thus, it will not fail to be precise and correct.
Nevertheless, regarding the wondrous principle of the green bamboos and yellow flowers, there still remains a lack of the essential pivot.
Tell me, what is it ultimately like? "Scoop up water and the moon is in your hand; pluck a flower and its fragrance fills your robe.
Foguo said, "The taste of the fragrant bait on the hook—the intent lies with the dragon in the azure depths. Indeed, he leaps over the waves and overturns the billows.
His horns are already manifest; no net can ensnare him, and no call can bring him back. Had it not been for Old Man Tongan, his fishing pole would surely have been lost.
When Master Jue asked a monk, "The realm of the eye has no light; how can one see? the monk replied, "The Big Dipper turns to the east."
Nan-dou moved westward. Chan-cha said, "When the Master enters the Grand Ancestral Temple.
The monk said, "In that case, under Tong-an, the Way has been cut off and the people have vanished. Chan-cha said, "Cradling an infant across one's chest, intending to manifest the imperial decree."
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "This monk understands how to tend the rootless tree and is able to lift the lamp from the bottom of the sea;
he is much like one who ascends the Yu Gate, shaking out his scales and fins. Yet, though the waves strike him at a depth of a thousand fathoms, alas, the Dragon King pays him no heed."
Zhengjue said, "A common colloquialism; Tong'an could have said even more.
Fohai said, "The essential core of a patriarch: casting an iron tortoise into a great furnace.

When the adept monk’s wheel of mechanism turns, the earth is overturned, the heavens are turned upside down, and the stars revolve. Were it not for such a master of the school, he could not have netted these outstanding monks."

Zhengjue said, "The large and the small are equally at ease; in the end, they do not recognize this monk. It was a scene of swallowing one's voice and quenching one's breath.

Foguo held up his whisk and said: "This monk pressed Tongan so hard that he was left with no way to turn his body;

To cite an instance from when Dongshan was traveling on pilgrimage: while reading the records of National Teacher Zhong, he came across a monk’s question:
“What is the mind of the ancient Buddha? The National Teacher replied, “Walls, tiles, and pebbles. The monk asked, “Are walls, tiles, and pebbles not insentient?
The National Teacher said, “They are. The monk asked, “Can the insentient also preach the Dharma? The National Teacher replied, “They constantly preach; they preach with blazing intensity.”

[The monk] asked without pause, "Who is it that can hear [this]? The National Teacher said, "All the sages can hear it. The monk asked, "Does the Master also hear it? The National Teacher said, "I do not hear it.
The monk asked, "If the Master does not hear it, how do you know that insentient things are capable of preaching the Dharma?
The National Teacher said, "It is fortunate that I do not hear it. If I were to hear it, I would be equal to the sages. You..."
[The monk] said, "In that case, they would not hear me preach the Dharma. The National Teacher said, "I preach for the sake of sentient beings;
I do not preach for the sake of the sages. The monk asked, "After sentient beings have heard it, what then? The National Teacher said:

[He] was then no longer a sentient being. Later, [Zhao]zhou arrived at Mount Gui. Guishan asked, "Master Jia, is it true that you harbor doubts regarding the National Teacher’s teaching of the insentient?
Zhaozhou said, "It is. Guishan said, "Try to bring it up for me to see. Zhaozhou then recounted the previous circumstances.
Guishan said, "I have this as well here, but it is rare to meet someone capable of it. Zhaozhou said, "Please do so then. Guishan thereupon—
[He brandished] the whisk. [Dongshan] said, "Give me a single point. Mount Shishuang said, "I ask the Master to explain it for me.

Mount Shishuang said, "The mouth born of one's parents shall never speak for one's own child. Dongshan said, "In this place of yours, Master, are there any others of the same age who aspire to the Way?
Mount Shishuang said, "Going from here to Liling Youxian, there is Yunyan, whose dwelling is connected to the Stone Chamber."
"O man of the Way, if you can brush away the grass to perceive the wind, you will surely value this.

When Guishan went to Yunyan to seek further instruction, Yunyan said, "Have you not seen it stated in the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* that 'the water birds and the forest trees all constantly recollect the Buddha, recollect the Dharma, and recollect the Sangha'?
Because of this, Guishan attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "How truly marvelous! How truly marvelous! The insentient preach the Dharma!"
Inconceivable! If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to comprehend; only when hearing through the faculty of sight does one finally know.
Foguo (Foguo Weibai) held up his staff and said: "The heavens are high and the earth is deep; the seas are vast and the mountains are distant.

If you wish to exhaustively fathom the source, you must possess sharp faculties and superior wisdom. Dongshan, an ancient Buddha, harbored doubts throughout his life regarding this matter of "insentient beings preaching the Dharma."
The conditions are such that one’s eyes can no longer see one’s own nostrils. This is because one’s intellectual understanding is sharp and clever, and profound mysteries dwell within one's breast;
thus, one divides the insentient and the sentient into two segments, and treats hearing and not hearing, speaking and not speaking, as two distinct types.
Yet when it comes to the final end, the bottom of the bucket falls out, and only then does one realize that the nostrils have been on the face all along. Today, this mountain monk—
They do not avoid mud and water; they go to the heavy assemblies. The National Teacher’s stone pillar sprouts branches;
Daowei’s pestle-head produces flowers; Yunyan saws apart a cast-iron weight. Having exhausted all spiritual powers, they achieve this unperforated iron stake.
Do you understand? When a thousand layers of locks are gone, a single sword leans against the cold heavens.

The monk said, "In the end, the pointing was not mistaken. Jingfeng asked, "What is this matter of 'not being mistaken'?"
The monk held up his hand like a mountain peak and pointed to himself again. The Peak asked, "Have you ever seen the former master? The monk asked, "Where would one see him?
The Peak replied, "One sees him where one eats rice porridge and meals. The monk circumambulated the meditation seat once, and the Peak closed the door of the abbot’s quarters.
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "In Pūrvavideha they sing songs; in Jambudvīpa they perform dances;
in Aparagoyānī they clap their hands; in Uttarakuru they beat drums. What a magnificent musical performance! Why is it so?"
"It is simply because he once met the former master.
Zhengjue said, "The canopies are tilted together; the true mechanism is exchanged. Do not take it amiss that this is the livelihood of our house;
from the beginning, the lineage has been clear. As for this monk, when he circumambulates the meditation seat, one can know it; Jinfeng’s closing of the door is [the proof]."
What do they await? Do you understand? In our house, there are no conventional rites.
Fogu said: "One person holds a probing pole in hand; another carries a blade of grass for his shadow.
Not only are they born of the same lineage, they shall also die of the same lineage. But how can one discern this? When he saw the former master coming, he opened his eyes.
It is also right. It is also right with eyes closed.
[The Master] cites Gold Peak (Jinpeak) Worthy: as soon as a monk entered the abbot’s quarters, Gold Peak struck him. The monk said, “Right, right. Gold Peak struck him again.
The monk said, “Not right, not right. Gold Peak made a gesture of bowing; the monk made a gesture of pushing away. Gold Peak said, “Old monk...”
The monk said, "Your eyesight is dim. Xuefeng replied, "The *ācārya*’s hearing is impaired. The monk said, "If you bring food to feed the fish, you must still practice self-restraint.

Xuefeng said, "By offering food, one receives the retribution of long life. The monk asked, "How old is the Master? Xuefeng said, "It does not fall within the range of numerical calculation. The monk asked, "Who is it that possesses long life?
Xuefeng said, "Jin-feng. The monk said, "Indeed, your eyesight is blurred. Xuefeng said, "Right you are, right you are."
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "With a mechanism beyond the mundane, he employs a function beyond the mundane. Banners and streamers interlace; cavalry and infantry join ranks.
A great battle is waged until even the mulberry tree is struck by an arrow and the willow tree exudes sap.
Although they emerge from the weeds and enter the weeds, victory and defeat remain undifferentiated. Do you understand this thoroughly? It is the mechanism of mutual exchange. Subhūti.
Examine this closely.
Zhengjue said: "If there were no retribution for good and evil, then Heaven and Earth would surely possess partiality.
Fohai said: "When these two people meet, it would be well to take a single wooden pole and carry them both as one load upon it, circling [the world]."

Mount Sumeru has been encircled hundreds of thousands of times, yet there is not the slightest bit of unevenness or deficiency. Why is this? Because those with blind eyes and deaf ears share the same condition of illness and pain.
Once, when Jinfeng saw the practitioner Bian approaching, he lifted up a sutra, made a gesture as if grasping his robes, and looked at him with his eyes.
Foguo added a comment: "The three apertures are all clear; Bian ti sits upon his sitting mat. He looked at Jinfeng with his eyes.
Foguo added a comment: "Both ends are cut off. Feng said, "Everyone says you understand Chan.
Foguo added a comment: "A mere smearing over. Bian asked, "How about you, Preceptor? Foguo added a comment: "Pushing it back again..."
"Can you do it? Feng laughed and said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated.
Foguo added a comment: "As expected. Foguo further picked up the point and said: "Jinpeak spreads flowers upon brocade; Bian the practitioner spreads brocade upon flowers.
However, this still obstructs the matter at hand. At that time, had he been a true man, when the other brought up the scripture, he would simply—"
He said to him: "What is it? From antiquity to the present day, you have served as a model; the Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury have all been expounded at once.
Zhengjue said:
"To deploy transformations according to the occasion is certainly granted to the old man of Jinfeng, yet he has already raised the flag of surrender and cannot be said to be satisfied."
The "Man on the Road" is here. Why? It is like wrapping a large tiger in a damp paper.
Master Fohai said: "The dragon rises from the vast ocean; the tiger emerges from the edge of the forest. It comes straight down—look quickly with your eyes!"
A monk asked Jinfeng, "The pivot that does not fall into the categories of sage or ordinary—please, Master, speak of it apart from these. Jinfeng said, "Jinfeng’s eyes are no small thing.
The monk said, "In that case, a single stroke on a fine lute suddenly clears the sovereign. Jinfeng said, "How could you possibly speak of it otherwise?
The monk said, "As for the words spoken for the sake of things, what then? Jinfeng said, "Suddenly clearing the sovereign. The monk said, "..."
"Not even Jinfeng would find this easy. Jinfeng said, "A man of fine strategy; even with a full seat at the banquet, he still falls short.
The monk said, "If you do not acknowledge these words, I fear you will fall into delusion. Jinfeng said, "Acknowledge what words? The monk said, "Why trouble yourself to repeat them?
Jinfeng said, "A mute person chasing a boat—how much more stubborn and dull-witted!"
Foguo held up his staff and said: "Releasing and gathering in, it seems severed yet continues; seizing the flag and taking the drum, it is like rolling up yet unfolding again.
Although this is presented face-to-face, nevertheless both parties suffer defeat.
But tell me, where exactly is the place of their defeat?"

Zhengjue said, "The Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment and the Separate Path of Jinfeng: though their ways differ, they reach the same destination. This monk accepted the words; he was respectful but lacked propriety.
Although he attained immediate clarity regarding the Sovereign Lord, he still fell into confusion and was deluded by the stubborn and ignorant.
Foguo said, "Though it was presented face-to-face, both parties nonetheless suffered a loss. But tell me, where exactly was the loss?"—Jinfeng.
"That is far too much.
Fogu said, "This monk possesses a pivot that does not fall into the categories of sage or ordinary person.
Were it not for Jinfeng possessing the eye that does not fall into the categories of sage or ordinary person, he would often be led astray and confused by this mute man."
Juejin once saw a monk sweeping the floor. Juejin asked, "What are you doing? The monk held up his broom.
Juejin said, "There is still this remaining. The monk asked, "What did you see just now, Master? Juejin then picked up his staff.
Foguo picked up the case and said: "Great and small Jinfeng still act with such reservations. At that time, had he waited for him to say, 'What have you seen, Master?
and then struck him across the back with his staff? Why? Because to kill a man one must see blood;
to benefit others one must go to the very end."
Zhengjue says: "This monk’s broom, Jinfeng’s staff, the shadow-grass and the probing pole—beating the void to produce a sound;
there is still this one remaining. Yijie said, "Rare indeed!"
Buddha-Haiyun said: "To see it and not grasp it; to contemplate it from a thousand miles away—both are equally direct encounters with the wind and regulations [of the Dharma].
It is a pity to let such a move slip by.
He cited the case where one day Jingu Peak saw a monk approaching, stood up immediately, and as the monk departed, the Peak said, "Just as I..."
Yesterday, a monk failed to distinguish the meaning of my words. The monk turned back and asked, "What did the monk say yesterday?
Feng said, "I was just asking that. The monk said, "I know that Jin-feng has eyes. Feng said, "Setting aside Jin-feng for a moment, where will you eat your meal today?
The monk said, "If I were to penetrate it, it would not be right. Feng said, "In that case, there is no place from which you have come."
The monk said, "It is the mind of an old woman; what can it do? Fēng said, "When Jīnfēng questioned the monk, he did not weaken him.
Among them, you, Reverend, have no place for words. The monk said, "How could this be considered going beyond one's bounds? Fēng said, "Small kindness obstructs great kindness."
Foguo held up his staff and said: "The fragrant bait on the hook is cast out and drawn back; the scaled dragon of brocade breaks through the waves, shaking its whiskers and tossing its fins.
Although Jinguo Peak never weakened him, alas, this monk weakened himself by following the cue. Do you understand?
A small kindness obstructs a great kindness."
Zhengjue said, "Since you already know that this small compassion obstructs great compassion, for what reason did you let it pass until matters reached this state?
It is simply because yesterday’s and today’s affairs are not the same."
Fohaiyun once remarked: "I have heard that at the Golden Peak Pass, few people have ever been able to pass through. Yet this monk has gone from door to door;
even if one were to bring out a staff to intercept him, one could not stop him. Tell me, has he passed the pass yet?"
Master Jingfeng raised his hand upon seeing a monk approach and said, "This is the business of a great man.
Try to deliver a message for me. The monk said, "I do not wish to deceive you, Master. Jingfeng said, "One who knows how to practice filial piety is truly rare indeed.
The monk asked, "Is this not the business of a great man? Jingfeng replied, "It is the old monk [who speaks]."
"I do not wish to deceive you, Ācārya. The monk said, "When one reaches this point, it is not easy to discern clearly.
Feng said, "Quite so, quite so. The monk bowed. Feng asked, "From where did you set out? The monk said, "Right here.
Feng said, "Not only do you deceive yourself, but you also deceive me, the old monk."
Foguo held up the staff and said: "In the house of a master of the school, both 'knocking' and 'singing' are practiced; both the provisional and the real are illuminated. Both parties are masters;
neither wishes to deceive the other, and thus they achieve filial nourishment and manifest the marks of a great man.
Since this is so, why did Jinfeng at the very end not let it pass? Do you understand? If you do not pay the price, [you will not receive it]."
They debated the truth and falsehood [of the statement].
Zhengjue said, "Although this monk deceived Jinfeng, he spoke the truth; he should repent.
Fohai said, "Jinfeng raised his hand once, and the Three Worthies lost their courage while the Ten Sages were struck with terror. Why is it that the two..."
He turned back three times, deceiving one another. Have you not heard it said: "This is the affair of a great man"?
Jingu Peak addressed the assembly, saying: "The fact exists as the lid fits the box; the principle should be like the point of an arrow meeting its target. Is there anyone who can say this?
If there were someone who could say it, Jingu Peak would divide his monastery in half and give it to him to dwell in. At that time, a monk came forward and prostrated.
He bowed. Feng said, "It is easy to meet, but it is difficult to live together for others' sake.
He then descended from his seat. Foguo took up the case, saying: "How great is Da Jin-feng! His head is that of a dragon, but his tail is that of a snake.
If it were Jiangshan, it would not be so. If anyone can say something [to this], I, the mountain monk, shall divide half my monastery with him to dwell in. Suddenly, there was one who came forth..."
When he came to pay his respects, [Jinpeng] simply said to him: "Ascending to heaven, we return together to the Milky Way; entering the earth, we return together to the Yellow Springs. Zhengjue said:
"Ordinarily, many say that this monk was too hasty in his progress and that Jinpeng’s earlier words did not accord with his later ones.
But this is not so. Why? Have you not heard it said: 'The matter exists as the lid fits the box; the principle corresponds to the arrow's flight'?"
"Arrow-points meeting.
Foguo Haiyun said, "Jin-feng has only the mind to receive the jade tablet, yet lacks the intention to divide the city. Jiangshan is not so;
in his case, the matter exists as the fitting of a lid upon a box, and the principle should be like the meeting of arrow-points. If you can speak it, then both hands are divided.

only when faced with difficulty does one see the mind of a true man.

The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall follow it accordingly. Feng asked, "What do you call it? The monk said, "A pillow. Feng said, "..."
"He has fallen into the hollow of the Golden Peak.
Foguo held it up and said: "A whole mass without seams or cracks; so dense and continuous that not even a breeze can pass through. One cannot paint it, nor can one depict it."
No matter how much you try to mold it, you cannot form it; yet to call it a "pillow" is already to fall into the trap of Jinfeng.
Even if you do not call it a pillow, you still cannot escape falling into Jinfeng’s trap. So, how can one emerge from Jinfeng’s lair?
Recognize the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not fixate on the zero point of the scale.

The Clouds of Perfect Enlightenment: Within the Gold Peak’s Hollow, there is no confusion or error. When the pillow is picked up, do you understand? With a single cry from the returning wild goose, the spring dream is severed;
only then does one realize that body and world are but a realization of the Southern Branch.
Buddha-Ocean Cloud: To lift up the whole lump is a fine standard; even "flashing like a spark" is already too late.
Without falling into the nest of Jingfeng, one must seek advantage with empty hands.
A monk asked Jinfeng, "What is the true master of Jinfeng? Jinfeng said, "The town and county are not far from here;
do not act so hastily, *ācārya*. The monk said, "Why did you not say [anything]? Jinfeng said, "Your mouth is a foundation stone."
Foguo held up the staff and said: "Jinpeak’s solitary wind is chillingly majestic. This monk dares to pull at the tiger's whiskers.
Although he may strike back from a thousand miles away, he still falls short by a single thread. At that moment, had I waited for him to ask, 'What is the true master of Jinpeak?
I would have struck him on the spot as soon as he spoke. Why? To test jade, it must pass through fire; to seek pearls, one does not leave the mud."
Zhengjue said, "It is easy to open a mouth from beginning to end, but difficult to preserve a heart through the cold of winter.
Fohai said, "What need is there for this monk's prolixity? He should simply pay one prostration toward the place where Jinfeng first gave his answer."
To stroke a tiger’s whiskers is also one’s own proper duty.
A monk asked Jinfeng, "What is it like when a golden cup is filled to the brim? Jinfeng said, "Jinfeng is more than tipsy."
Foguo held up his staff and said: "To understand the source by following words and to respond universally according to one's capacity is not without merit—there is indeed Jin-feng.
Yet, if one examines it closely, there is still much that is leaked away. If someone were to ask Jiangshan, 'What is it like when a golden cup is filled to the brim?
I would simply answer him: 'This mountain monk has always been under Heaven’s admonition.'"
Zhengjue said, "A red face is not as good as straightforward speech.
Fohai said, "Riding the thief’s horse, chasing the thief’s band.
The master Jinfeng asked a monk, "Where did you set out from? The monk replied, "Zhaozhou. Jinfeng asked, "Whose Dharma heir was Zhaozhou?"
The monk said, “Nanquan. Feng said, “When did you ever leave Zhaozhou? The monk said, “I do not know what your honorable intention is, Master.
Feng said, “Zhaozhou will certainly succeed Nanquan. That evening, the monk again requested further instruction, saying, “Today I have received the Master’s compassion, yet I have not yet understood.
I beg the Master to point it out once more. Feng said, “If you go elsewhere...”
[The Master] said, "Do not say that the later words are from the bottom of Jingu Peak. The monk asked, "Why is it so? Jingu Peak said, "I fear it would bring shame upon Zhaozhou.
Foguo took up this case and said, "Although this monk came from Zhaozhou, he missed Zhaozhou’s pivot right before his face. It was empty."
To send him to Jinfeng required so much hammering and forging; yet, in the end, it was simply for him to meet Zhaozhou—it had nothing to do with this monk’s own business.
Does the assembly know where the point lies? It is clearly the path behind the arrow.
Zhengjue Yun said, "The fool eats a punch from a simpleton.
Fohai Yun said, "A Persian enters a bustling market.

"Humanity," [Feng] said, "I have a karmic anecdote to relate to you. The monk made a gesture as if listening. Feng struck him with his palm.
The monk asked, "Why did you strike me? Feng replied, "I want this story to circulate."

[Kan-iao] none of them know. Tell me, where does it fall? Six ears do not share a secret."
Zhengjue said, "Do not hand over the golden needle to others.

Fohai said, "Jinpeak would have flayed it alive and swallowed it whole. Had he used this monk at the outset, if that monk had any backbone in his eyes, he likely would not have been willing to swallow his voice and suppress his spirit."

Jinfeng stepped down from his meditation seat, grabbed the monk by the ears, and twisted them. The monk let out a cry of pain. Jinfeng said, "Today, for the first time, I have caught hold of this ignorant fellow.

Foguo held up his staff and said: "This monk threw a brick to draw out jade; Jinfeng entered the grass to seek a man.
