Fohai said, "The face and eyes of Jinfeng are right before you; what can be done? It is like dying without being mourned."
Jin-feng called out to a monk, "Do you know Jin-feng’s single phrase? The monk replied, "I have known it for a long time. Jin-feng asked, "How so?
The monk then gave a shout and said, "Jin-feng’s single phrase—today it is shattered into a hundred pieces! Jin-feng said, "You have indeed been asking others about this;
among them, you, Reverend, are the most rigorous in your school's style. The monk said, "It cannot be that one must necessarily rely on another."
Feng checked him. Feng said, "Brass does not equal gold.
Foguo took it up, saying, "Jinpeng drags through the mud; this monk wades through the water.
Although he was earnest at the end, alas, he missed the mark right at the beginning."
Zhengjue said, "He has fallen! He has fallen!
Foguo commented, "This monk let him off at the beginning, but was insistent at the end. This is the way one studies the fundamental matter;
he simply drove him away like that. What need is there to speak of 'Jin-feng’s One Phrase'? Nevertheless, even fine jade must pass through the fire."
Jin’gong asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk stepped forward and remained silent for a long while. Jin’gong said, “What person have you gone to visit, *ācārya*?
The monk said, “Visiting what bowl? Jin’gong said, “Jin’gong has committed an offense. The monk said, “Indeed, indeed. Jin’gong remained silent for a long while.

Foguo held up his whisk and said: "This monk remained silent for a long time—this is like hiding a lamp in a dark room. Jinfeng remained silent for a long time—this is like the lamp being hidden within the dark room.
Although it is true that 'receiving an ox from one person, returning a horse to another,' nevertheless, while the front is aligned, the back has not yet met face-to-face.
Ultimately, how is it? Within the jar, there is a separate heaven and earth."
Zhengjue said, "Do you understand? If you do, then jade and stone are distinguished; if you do not, then jade and stone are burned together.
Fohai said, "When Jinyong met this monk, it was like the clear blue sky where clouds suddenly arise and rain pours down, saturating everything high and low.
After a long silence, Jinyong remained silent with this monk for a long while. How about that? Rest.
He asked again for the way back, to which [the master] replied, "This very place is Penglai.
He then cited Master Jingong: when a monk arrived and was just about to exchange greetings, Jingong said, "There is no need to offer seasonal pleasantries."
The first phrase: "Bring it forth. The monk said, "It is still cold in the early spring; I humbly wish the Master ten thousand blessings in your health.
Feng said, "There is still this [subject] remaining. The monk said, "One must not require someone else to examine it.
Feng asked, "Who? The monk pointed at himself with his hand. Feng said, "It is no hindrance to be examined by others."
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "Although this monk is skilled at discerning the winds and clouds, what can he do against Jinfeng snatching the flag and seizing the drum?
Do you understand? Have you not heard it said: 'He studies the living word, not the dead word'?"
Zhengjue said, "It cannot be the first phrase.
Fohai said, "If you can speak it, you will not escape being scrutinized by others; if you cannot speak it, you likewise will not escape being scrutinized by others.
Pointing to his own body, he asked: 'Who is this? When the Sleeping Dragon has not yet turned his body, [he remains thus]."
A monk asked Master Fenghuang, "He sits atop the crown of Vairocana and does not receive the teachings of Śākyamuni.
I wonder, with whom does this person take as companions? Fenghuang said, "Struck through with a single stroke. The monk said, "If that is so, then it is rare to encounter one who understands.
Fenghuang said, "First, look closely. The monk said, "If it is thus, I shall pay my respects and depart. Fenghuang said, "Furthermore..."

When [Zhaozhou] was serving [the Master], Foguo held up [his whisk] and said: "The eyes of a patriarch must reach such a state—like a bright mirror set upon its stand, like a luminous pearl held in the palm.
Sending it forth and withdrawing it, there is no further leakage. But tell me, what has he attained? Do you understand?"
Xima said: "Stick your head out beyond the heavens and look; who is this person within? Zhengjue said:
"To strive for it is insufficient; to yield to it leaves room for more.
Fohai said: "This monk asked about the head; although he seized the peak with a twist, it does not take even a single stroke to strike him down. (4)

Character. There is a distinct, wondrous function and spiritual power here that cannot be entered by means of conceptualization. Why? Because this house has long ago stepped upon the ultimate barrier.
A monk asked Wolong: "Set aside your attendants, and then I ask to see you. Wolong said: "Try to see with your eyebrows raised."
The monk asked, "When it is not like this, what then? Long said, "He has gone north of the mountain.
Foguo commented: "In the spark struck from flint, within the flash of lightning—there is the provisional and the real, there is contraction and expansion;
though it is indeed swift and brilliant, it nevertheless sticks to the skin and adheres to the bone. If I were Jiangshan, I would not do so."
Suddenly someone asked, "Please dismiss your attendants; I request to meet you, Master. He simply replied, "Go drink tea.
Zhengjue said, "I would wait until my head was soaked by the rain."
Buddha-Sea Cloud: When coming, his sharp fangs and claws are terrifying; when departing, he rushes swiftly toward the boundless directions.
A monk asked Yantou, "What is it like when one encounters a fierce tiger on the road? Yantou said, "Press! (Za).
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "The heavens have no four walls; the earth is cut off from the eight directions.
Even if one were to have ten thousand arrows piercing the heart and a thousand spears striking the body, one still could not withstand this single pivot. Do you understand?
Six times six is originally thirty-six."
Zhengjue said, "The great fruit of Buddhahood, whether large or small—originally, you have miscalculated.
Fohai said, "If one were to shed tears frequently enough, even the vast ocean would surely dry up."
A monk asked Yantou, "When a sharp sword cuts through the world, who is it that faces the blade? Yantou said, "Dark.
As the monk was about to offer further words, Yantou said, "Dull-witted fellow!"
Foguo held up his staff and said: "This is so, yet this 'living man's sword' has no place to be grasped. If it were Jiangshan, it would not be thus.
Suppose someone were to ask: 'A sharp sword slays the world; who is the one who faces it head-on?'"
He simply said to him, "I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.
Zhengjue said, "Foguo’s Way is a sword that brings people to life; it has no place to be grasped. Yet, what can one do about the person wielding the sword?
Fohai said, "This monk took up a single sword, intending to take the heads of all the people in the world, and arrived before Yantou."
[The Master] stepped forward. Why did he first strike? Because one who gives rise to an evil mind will, in turn, receive its calamity.
To cite the case of Master Yantou: when Sansheng came to visit him, Yantou said, "There is no need to spread out your sitting mat;
there is no leftover gruel or stale rice here. Sansheng said, "Even if there were, where would you put it? Yantou struck him. Sansheng caught the staff and pushed him away.
He threw it onto the bed. He struck his palm once. The Master (Sheng) covered his head with his sitting mat and went out, crying out to the blue heavens.
Fuguo commented: "Both were swift and decisive; each was skilled at seizing the drum and snatching the banner.
Yet both suffered defeat; they met blade for blade and hand for hand. It was much like climbing a high mountain while holding hands—one cannot help but be looked upon by the bystanders."
[The Master] laughed. He asked the assembly, "Who is the bystander?
Zhengjue said, "When a state-level man treats me with such honor, I repay him with a state-level response.
Fohai said, "Wisdom fights wisdom; valor fights valor; fist meets fist; kick meets kick. But tell me, who is it?"
The family style of the moon: it frightens old man Li of East Village.
A monk asked Master Xiangyan, "What is the Way? Xiangyan said, "A dragon’s cry within a withered tree. The monk said, "I do not understand.
Xiangyan said, "Eyes within a skull. The monk then asked Shishuang, "What is the withered tree?"
Longyin said, "The frosty clouds still carry a trace of joy. The monk asked, "What is the eye within the skull? Longyin said, "It still carries a trace of consciousness.
The monk then raised this question with Caoshan, who offered this verse: "The dragon’s cry from the withered tree is the true seeing of the Way."

The skull has no consciousness, yet its eyes first shine with clarity; when joyful consciousness is exhausted, all news and traces vanish. When one acts according to benevolence, how can one distinguish purity within turbidity?
The monk asked again: "What is the dragon’s cry within the withered tree? The Master said: "The life-blood is unbroken. The monk said: [further question].
"What are the eyes within the skull? Shanzhao replied, "Never exhausted.
Foguo commented: "Thoughts do not differ; the mind does not err. When the five stages of sovereign and subject are perfectly interfused, one leaps beyond the three poisons of the unconditioned.
Thus, one can cause flowers to bloom upon withered wood and blow the musical pipe amidst a cold cliff. Behold him!"
There were three old masters: one who had penetrated the leakage of words, one who had penetrated the leakage of emotion, and one who had penetrated the leakage of views.
If you can investigate and examine this well, you may walk alone upon the profound gateway. Do you understand? Do not linger by the cold crags where strange grasses turn green;
sit amidst the white clouds, for the essence of the school is not merely "wondrous."
The Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment asks: "Do you understand? Xiangyan gathers flowers; Shishuang makes honey; Caoshan boils tea.
Now tell me, who is it that knows the sweetness?"
Buddha-Sea Cloud: "If one's effort does not reach its limit, there will be no squareness or roundness; if one's words are not intimate, one is not a kinsman.
When the ancients reached this point and spoke from this point, they did not shift or alter even a single hair’s breadth. To examine it closely:
One person establishes himself on the profound path; another clears away the tracks of the birds. If Cao Shan were not present, both lineages would have been severed.
Yet another person remains unmoved in expression, standing by with hands in his sleeves as an observer.
If anyone can discern this and penetrate this koan, they shall understand.
There was once an old master who went to Linji’s place. When Linji saw him coming, he let out a shout. The old master said, “A double case. Linji asked, “Where does the fault lie?
The old master said, “This wild fox spirit! Linji then ceased speaking. Fuguo added a comment: “He has deceived an entire shipload of people!
The old master stepped forward, held up his sitting cloth, and said, “If you unfold it, it is this; if you do not unfold it, it is that...”
Ji said, "Yes. Sujiu then gave a shout. Xiusu then spread out his sitting mat. Ji said, "This thief! Xiusu then folded up his sitting mat and left with his sleeves brushed back.
Ji said, "Do not say you were without fault. Foguo added a comment: "He has been thoroughly seen through.
Ji turned his head and saw the Head Seat, so he asked him, "What do you say? Was there a fault just now, or was there not? The Head Seat said, "There was a fault. Ji said, [and continued].

The guest’s house had committed a fault; the host’s house had committed a fault. Linji said, "Both have committed faults. Nanquan asked, "Where does the fault lie? Linji shook his sleeves and departed.

Nanquan said, "Do not say it was 'no affair. Fuguo added a comment: "He has been thoroughly seen through. Later, a monk cited this to Nanquan, asking, "I do not know what the intent of these three men was. Nanquan said: "Linji’s words were like a sharp sword; he struck directly at the source. Nanquan’s words were like a heavy hammer; he brought down the final blow.

As for the monk who raised the question, he was like a blind man pointing at the moon—he could not see it himself and could not let others see it either. If you can discern where the fault lies, you will understand the meaning of these three men. If you cannot, you must still seek it out yourself."
"It is much like official horses trampling one another. Foguo added a comment, saying, "He has been thoroughly scrutinized.
Foguo further remarked, "In general, a master of the school must possess the diamond-like correct eye (*vajra-cakṣus*) before he can manifest such a strategic maneuver.
It is just as when I, this mountain monk, applied three 'scrutinies' below. If you wish to penetrate and clarify [this], [you must look at] Lin..."
To uphold the true eye and circulate the Great Teaching, one must surely grasp this. If it is not yet so, do not say that it is well to remain in a state of non-action.
Zhengjue said: "I have thoroughly seen through you."
Buddha-Samudra-Cloud said: "In his daily practice, Linji strikes amidst the flash of lightning and the spark of a flint;
today this old master is capable of acting as host and skilled at playing the guest. His advances and retreats accord with propriety, and his dynamic functions are merged in harmony."
One can do nothing but agree with the Head Seat and let the matter pass for the time being. When one arrives before Master Wang, it merely results in official horses trampling one another.
It is said that when Master Furi arrived at Jingshan, Shan asked: "I have heard that you, Elder, dwell alone in a certain place; why is that?"

Dayu then asked Jingshan, "'The hidden and the manifest are fully encompassed; people of the time know this exists, yet they cannot speak of it.

Daowu asked, "How is it to speak of the Way oneself, or to speak of the Way as being intimate with the Way? Mount Yunmen said, "In my house, where the Way is practiced, there is nothing to speak of.

Dayu said, "On the path of the Tathāgata, there is no partiality or crookedness. Please, let us harmonize one more note of the profound sound. Yunmen said, "Let the two wheels shine upon each other as they may;
beyond the azure sky and outside the clouds, they do not interfere with one another. Dayu said, "I report this to the infinite multitude of white-haired elders: this time, the year..."
Shao said, "Do not return to your hometown. Mount Yun said, "Old and young are of the same kind; there is no partiality between them. The profound path of one house is without discrepancy.
Dayu said, "A single word settles the world; for whom are the four lines intended? Mount Yun said, "You say there are three or four; I say that even the one in their midst does not exist.
Dayu then prostrated. Mount Yun then offered this verse: "Even east and west he does not look back; south..."
"With whom does the north neighbor? You say there are three or four; I say that not even one of them exists.

The Buddha-fruit (Foguo) held up his whisk and said: "Possessing eyes that transcend the school and surpass the standard, and a capacity that is peerless and measureless—to encounter [the guest] suddenly on the road is truly extraordinary.

Mingzhong sat with his tongue hanging out.

Where there is nothing that can be spoken of, one speaks; this is not an impediment, for it is secretly all-encompassing.
It reaches the point where old and young are of the same rank, a single family’s mysterious path. Disregarding east and west, who is a neighbor to the south or north?

At Tiantai Guoqing Temple, Master Shan said, "I have heard that in Tiantai there are murmuring streams and shimmering waves.
You, Xie, have come from afar; what is your intention? Master Ri replied, "I have long dwelt among the crags and valleys, unattached to the pines and vines. Master Shan said:
"This is still the meaning of spring. As for the meaning of autumn, how is it? After a long silence, Shanshan said, "I see you are merely a passenger rowing a boat;
in the end, you are not a man who can play in the tide. Day then withdrew.

When two elders meet like overturned canopies, their voices and countenances are composed and at ease; these two venerable seniors have attained this in abundance.
As for the matter of praise and blame in this exchange: let us set aside for now the initial arrangement made beneath the bright window.
At the end, it is said, "One who is not a master of the tide has departed from the Buddha-sun. Now tell me, was he content or not?
Try to judge.
Buddha-Haiyun: Without the strength to lift a cauldron or pull up a mountain, how could one urge on a ten-thousand-li black steed?

Without the mechanism to turn heaven and shift earth, how could one control the cloud-winged steeds suspended in the sky? The gates and walls of Jia Shan are as perilous as a mountain and as deep as the sea;
before the Buddha-Sun has even ascended the steps, one has already encountered his interrogation. Observe how he gallops like a dragon and bounds like a tiger.
The jade turns and the pearl revolves; there is a beginning and an end, yet neither gain nor loss. As for those at the end who seek understanding through words, they say:
"Without the spring breeze, the flowers do not bloom; once the flowers have bloomed, they are blown down by the wind.
I dare ask: when the Buddha-sun has set, what then?
Once, while Jia Shan was engaged in communal labor, the Rector (Vina) ordered Furì to deliver some tea.

Fuguo took this up and said: "Zhu Xi was under attack from all eight directions, so he had to accommodate people with circuitous speech.
National Teacher Shao’s single move was timely, yet it could not avoid merely echoing empty sounds. At that moment, he should have waited for him to say, 'Do not strike me.'"
The story remains as it was. But tell him this: "In the future, you must surely encounter the right person.
Zhengjue said, "How great and small is Foguo! He applies his strength to the handle of an axe."
Buddha-Haizun said, "If it had not been for the clever mouse, I would have been bitten to death.
He then cited National Teacher Shao: When the Teacher arrived at Lumeng, Lumeng asked, "Where have you recently departed from?

The Teacher replied, "Guyin. Last night I stayed overnight at Layman Pang’s cave. Lumeng asked, "Among the five eyes, which one is the true eye? The Teacher replied, "I have long admired [your reputation]."
Lumen said, "This entire plot of land—what business is it of yours? The Master asked, "Where is the point of the question?
Foguo commented: "Although National Teacher Shao possessed the correct eye, he was nonetheless carrying a lock and a shackle.
Although Lumen acted as the master of this plot of land, he likewise had not yet found a place to entrust it. At that time...
Wait for him to ask, "Where is the pivot of the discourse? and reply to him, "The *ācārya* did not find a place to stay last night.
Wait for him to hesitate, and then strike him across the back with the staff. Why? Because even in that which is not elegant, there is elegance.
Zhengjue said, "These two old masters do not scratch where it does not itch, nor do they itch where it does not itch.
Fohai said, "Recognizing the head-word and possessing the true eye is more than sufficient;
why then do you say, 'What business is this patch of ground of yours?'"
Master Zhuxi asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Guangnan.
Zhuxi said, "Are there any extraordinary venerable elders there? The monk said, "As for extraordinary venerable elders, no one speaks of them.
There is only one person who is utterly shameless. Zhuxi said, "Who is it? The monk pointed at Zhuxi. Zhuxi said, "Indeed, he is shameless. The monk [departed].
The monk said, "If it were not for Zhuxi, people would be at a loss. Zhuxi covered his nose with his hand.
The monk stepped forward; Zhuxi struck him. The monk said, "Exactly so! Zhuxi replied, "This old monk’s administrative duties are many. The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed.
Zhuxi laughed heartily and said, "Lotus roots on the flat rock."
Foguo held up his staff and said: "When the opportunity arises, he points directly face-to-face; when face-to-face, the opportunity is seized with swiftness.
This monk has indeed stepped upon the pivotal bolt of the ultimate realm. Were it not for Zhuxi, who could have discerned his place of origin?
Do you all know the essential point? A lotus root on a flat rock."
Zhengjue said: "A guest who parts the weeds and gazes at the wind; when the sharp point of his wit comes like a split arrow, the lotus on the *pantā* rock blooms with iron flowers overnight.
Fohai said: "A marvelous old venerable one; a person of great shamelessness. The lotus on the *pantā* rock—how joyful!"
Seeing something quite new, he brought up the case of Master Micang.
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Taihu in Jizhou.
Micang said, "When you were coming here, what did Taihu say to you? The monk replied, "He told me that the road to Micang is steep. Micang said, "..."
"Having arrived here, what then? The monk said, "It is no different from the road when first setting out.
Cang said, "The Acharya has already failed Lake Tai. The monk said, "I, too, do not agree with the Master speaking in this way.
Cang said, "When you came, the road was steep; now the road is level. The monk said, "This path of the Master is indeed unimpeded. Cang said, "Lacquer."
"A fellow from the bucket—what limit is there to him?
Foguo took it up and said: "Gathered before words, released after phrases; each reflects the other, each meets the occasion.
Yet, alas, they only know how to walk the path of longevity; they do not know how to turn at the place where breath ceases. How can this be?"
If you can utter a single phrase that leaves us no cause for regret, you shall ascend the azure clouds with level steps.
Zhengjue said: "To clutch the head and seize the feet—there is indeed a reason for this. Yet when it comes to severing ties at the very end, one collapses inside a lacquer bucket.
Do not blame me for saying what I say; the road to Mice Granary is steep."
At the gate of Fohaiyun, before the entrance of Taihu and in front of Micang, to continue the lineage in such a manner is truly difficult to find.
It is precisely because one levels out the steep heights that one becomes a mere fellow of the lacquer bucket.
Master Pingtian saw a monk approaching and struck him. The monk stepped forward and seized the staff. Pingtian said, "Just now you were too hasty.
The monk snatched the staff away and struck Pingtian instead. Pingtian said, "A true adept! A true adept! The monk bowed. Pingtian stepped forward and made a gesture as if to snatch the staff;
the monk laughed heartily, shook out his sleeves, and departed. Pingtian said, "The grass-robber has been utterly defeated."
Foguo held up his staff and said: "When literature comes, respond with literature; when martial arts come, respond with martial arts; when fists come, respond with fists;
when kicks come, respond with kicks. This is no easy matter. A great battle rolls across the earth, yet alas, in the end, he loses by one move.
Do you understand? Even if you are as vast as the heavens, you must still rise from the ground; even if you are higher than the clouds, what can you do against the existence of Heaven?"
Zhengjue said, "Do you understand? Even if the general achieves total victory, when he returns, he will still lack the person who went forth.
Fohai said, "When the two houses meet, it is like fire meeting fire; their nature of heat is one, and the blazing flames are no different."
When employed, it is luminous; when concealed, it is obscure. [The Master] then held up his whisk and said:
"Is there no one here who would pluck the tiger's whiskers and sweep away in a single motion? The grass-robbers are utterly defeated!
Regarding the Venerable Master Dunru of Baima in the Western Capital: he asked a monk, "What is your name? The monk replied, "I cannot find a name.
Dunru said, "Since you are an old monk like me, I do not recognize good from bad. The monk said, "How many people have reached this point and remained in a state of bewilderment?
Dunru said, "Truly, you are a master. The monk said, "It must be through the Master’s eye that one attains it. Dunru said, "Dharma brother."
"Di-nü. The monk then went out. Ru called out, "Ācārya! The monk turned his head back. Ru said, "Words of bitter grievance."
"It is not difficult to speak out against this.
Foguo took up the case and said: "This monk indeed possesses the true eye; it was not right for him to turn his head back immediately.

Bai Ma’s fundamental hook and awl are truly difficult to encounter when one is in a hurry. Do you understand? When scolding each other, I spare you the jabbing of the beak. When they scolded each other...
"Spittle! You drench me with water!
The Perfectly Awakened One said: "This monk was fortunate enough to fly high and soar far, refusing to be caught in a net.
But when he was called by name and turned his head, he was much like a *xingxing* ape caught on a leash and intoxicated."
Buddha-Haiyun: "The white horse has eyes all over its body; this monk has his eyes all over his body.
When examined closely, it is quite laughable. What is there to laugh at? Words of bitter grievance are indeed difficult to utter.
Regarding Master Baoshou: Once, while a monk was coming to pay his respects, Baoshou said, "The hundreds of thousands of sages are all contained within this abbot’s quarters.
The monk asked, "As for what the ancients said—that the great chiliocosm is but a bubble on the ocean—where, then, does this abbot’s quarters reside?
Baoshou replied, "The thousand sages are present right now. The monk asked, "Who can testify to this?"
Zhaozhou then cast down his whisk. The monk moved from east to west and stood there; Zhaozhou struck him.
The monk said, "If one had not studied for a long time, how could one know the ultimate point? Zhaozhou replied, "Thirty years from now, these words will spread far and wide."
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "Baoshou set out his nets and spread his snares within the abbot’s quarters.
This monk, carrying horns upon his head, came charging through the waves three times; yet three times he was caught in the trap.
But tell me, what did he gain? Do you understand? Under a heavy reward, there must surely be brave men."
Zhengjue said: "Baoshou gave this instruction; the very point was for this monk to deliberate in this way. Although he understood how to deliberate in this way, what can be done?
It simply does not accord with the tally. Where is it that it does not accord with the tally?"
Thirty years later, when it was time for someone to examine them, Fohai said:
"Baoshou skillfully polishes jade; this monk is a brilliant gem without a flaw—cut and ground as fine as the finest stone."
"Like carving and like polishing. Now this teaching is widely practiced; why wait for thirty years later? To cite Master Xitang:
One day, during a communal work assignment (*pǔqǐng*), the Master gave this instruction: "The community, cause and effect are clearly evident."
"What can be done? What can be done? At that time, a monk came forward and propped his hands against the ground.
Linji asked, "What are you doing? The monk said, "Save me! Save me! Linji said, "Everyone, this monk is still somewhat capable.
The monk threw down his hoe, brushed out his sleeves, and ran off. Linji said, "A worm within the lion’s body eats the lion’s own flesh."
Foguo picked up the staff and said: "Xitang clearly understood the essential principles; from beginning to end, he fully upheld the orthodox command.

This monk acted like one of a different species, yet he failed to maintain his head while dragging his tail. I dare ask the assembly: cause and effect are manifestly clear—how do you express this in a single phrase?
If it is so, the Dragon Girl immediately attained Buddhahood; if it is not, Sunakṣatra fell into the abyss."
The Clouds of Perfect Enlightenment say: "When the wind comes, the grass moves; when the body acts, the shadow follows.
Cause and effect are clearly manifest. This is the perspective of such a person. Just as with this monk’s present retribution, where does one discern the cause?
If you can discern it, it will be clearly known. But if it is not yet so, what can be done? What can be done?"
Buddha-Haiyun: Having already swallowed the fragrant bait, he has now turned around and cast off the hook.
Yet his life and soul remain in the hands of Xitang. Regarding Master Yangshan: One day a foreign monk arrived. Yangshan drew the shape of a half-moon on the ground.
The monk stepped forward and added it to form a full circle. He then rubbed it away with his foot. Yangshan spread out both hands. The monk shook out his sleeves and departed.
Foguo picked up the case and said: "To pour lacquer into glue; to add salt to soy sauce. Their feathers and down are alike;
their physical forms are the same. Even so, the great and small Yangshan were both exposed by a foreign monk."
Zhengjue said, "This monk is quite persistent; he is trying to deceive me here in this land.
Fohai said, "When this monk had not yet left the Western Heavens, he deserved thirty blows. Now that he has arrived at Yangshan, he deserves another thirty blows.
You lofty students of the Way, try to look into this with your own eyes."
[The Record] relates that one day Yangshan suddenly saw a strange monk arrive through the air. The monk paid his respects and stood before him. Yangshan asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The monk said, "This morning I left West India. Yangshan said, "Why so late? The monk said, "I was traveling among the mountains and enjoying the waters.
Yangshan said, "As for supernatural powers and wondrous functions, you certainly possess them, Master; however, as for the Buddha-dharma, you must still return to it."
The old monk finally attained it. The monk said, "I came specifically to this eastern land to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet I have instead encountered a minor Śākyamuni.
He then took out a *bīḍa* leaf from Western India and presented it to the mountain, prostrated himself, and ascended into the sky upon the clouds, departing.
Foguo commented: "Driving the ox of the plowman; seizing the food of the hungry man—this has been the fang and teeth of those who have come before.
Yet this Arhat, though possessing such manifold supernatural powers and wondrous functions, stood before Yangshan with eyes staring and mouth agape. Why?
A crane may have its nine-fold gao, yet its wings find it hard to soar; a horse may lack the thousand-li stride, yet it vainly pursues the wind."
Zhengjue Yun said, "The Hu-mo monkey enters the cloth bag.
Fohai Yun said, "Yangshan snatches the food and drives the oxen; he even pats his chest, yet he is a man who is kicked by the feet in the void.
With just a light ladleful of foul water splashed upon him, he becomes despondent and withdraws. He called—
"Can one employ the wondrous function of supernatural powers through another's action?
[The Master] raised a case: A monk asked National Teacher Longji, "What is it like when a lion turns back and leaps?
Longji said, "Are you afraid of Mañjuśrī? The monk said, "Not only Mañjuśrī; even if a Buddha were to come, I would not look back. Longji said, "But what can you do about being caught by Mañjuśrī?"
"What does he ride? The monk said, "One who rides Mañjuśrī does not ride a lion. Jie said, "What about the matter of 'throwing it back'?
The monk said, "Its function is without deficiency. Jie said, "That is precisely Mañjuśrī riding a lion."
Foguo commented: "Words shot forth like arrows; once released, they cannot be diverted. Entering the ear, they have no root; once deep, they cannot be pulled out.
This monk presented his realization within the words before the enlightened master Longji, yet as soon as there was a single discrepancy in a word, he was brought low by him.
At that time, had he waited for [Longji] to ask, 'What about the matter of returning the throw? he would have—"
He overturned the meditation seat. Did you not hear it said: "The fragrant elephant rushes forward, losing its majesty; the devas and nāgas listen in silence, giving rise to joy"?
Zhengjue said: "Do not be surprised that he does not fear the Buddha; it is simply because his karma is heavy."
Buddha-Haiyun said: "I thought this was a lion being thrown back, only to be caught around the waist by Longji, who mounted him so that he could not turn over.
He then raised the case of a monk asking Master Shifeng, "What is the pearl in Dizang’s hand? Feng replied, "In your own hand."
"Is there anything more? A monk said, "I do not understand. Feng said, "Do not deceive the assembly. Feng then offered this verse:
Failing to recognize one's own treasure, One follows others in identifying external dust. Escaping one's shadow at midday, One loses one's head in the mirror.
Foguo remarked: "Although Master Shifeng enters the mud and the water to receive beings and benefit living creatures, he is much like one who relies on his power to deceive others.
Suppose someone were to ask Jingshan: 'What is the pearl in Dizang’s hand?'"
Simply say to him: "Is there anything left in your hand? If he says, "I do not know," tell him:
"This, rather, is the fault of this mountain monk. Why? Because the flower was not damaged, and even a bee may eat it."
Zhengjue said, "The mountain monk does not think so. If one were born as a nobleman, who would be sent to sell firewood and charcoal?
Fohai said, "This monk does not understand; it happened by mere chance. Even if you were to recognize the pearl in the palm of your hand..."
Ultimately, it is not like being "throughout the body.
A monk asked Master Laoguan, "What is the Vairocana Teacher? The Lord of the Dharma Body? Guān said, "I do not say."
The monk asked, "Why do you not speak? Guanzhi replied, "If I were to speak, I would have to shrink my tongue;
if I were not to speak, I would have to mute my mouth. The monk reported this to Dongshan. Dongshan spread out his sitting mat, prostrated, and said, "Ancient Buddhas!
Ancient Buddhas!"
Foguo held up [the whisk] and said: "To cast one's body across the mouth of a fierce tiger and to rub one's head against the head of a venomous snake requires a master of the school;
only then can such a method be employed. Had it not been for Dongshan, the situation would have been perilously close to being overlooked."
Do you know where it lands? It is said: "When one says the dawn has already broken, there are still those traveling by night.
Zhengjue said: "Had I known earlier that the lamp was fire, the rice would have been cooked long ago."
The Buddha-Ocean-Cloud: The Old Observer dwells within the mud and the water, emitting a great radiance. The Elder of Xinfeng calculates down to the very root.
He cites the case of Master Gushan: a monk from Silla came to visit him, and the Master said, "It is difficult to comprehend even directly; seeking it through words..."
"It becomes even more distant. If we speak of the Buddha and the Patriarchs, they are separated by the vastness of heaven and earth. Elder, how do you understand this? The monk was speechless.
He said to his attendant, "I do not understand. Please provide a turning phrase on my behalf. The attendant said:

"The Master speaks thus, yet he is still as far away as the ends of the earth," the monk said. When the monk reported this to Mount [Shan], the Master summoned his attendant and asked, "Did you provide that response on behalf of the newcomer?
Is it so? The attendant replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.
Foguo picked it up and said: "This monk merely receives echoes from empty space. The attendant clings to his old nest;
had he not encountered National Teacher Gushan, who drove the plowman’s ox and snatched the hungry man’s food, this fellow would have nearly established a monopoly on discourse. Do you understand?"
"The waves at Caoxi are just like those elsewhere; countless ordinary people sink beneath them.
Zhengjue said, "Attendant, when you spoke thus, yet when Gushan called you forward and questioned you, you immediately threw open your chest to accept the challenge.
You were beaten and expelled from the monastery. Tell me, were you willing or unwilling? Do you understand? The path ahead—"
The body is as light as a leaf; its lofty fame weighs more heavily than mountains for a thousand ages.
Foguo Hai said: "The National Teacher’s way of raising his son was too compassionate. When entering the weeds, how does it compare to the time of emerging from them?
Shooting through the nine layers of imperial palaces with a sacred arrow, he remains, as before, separated by the vast distance of heaven and earth."
To cite Master Xuefeng: One day, while walking with Xuansha, Xuefeng pointed to the ground before them and said, "On this plot of land, one could build a seamless stupa.
Xuansha asked, "How high would it be? Xuefeng looked up and down with his eyes.
Xuansha said, "The blessings and rewards of humans and devas are certainly not lacking for you, Master; however, as for the prophecy of Vulture Peak, I have never even dreamed of it."
Xuefeng said, "What do you say? Xuanzha replied, "Seven feet, eight feet.
Fuguo took this up and said, "If you seek supernatural powers and wondrous functions, you must study under Xuefeng.
If you seek a stable and secure ground, you must study under Xuanzha. Furthermore, there is one who does not involve either path; do you all understand? Sumeru..."
Striking the golden bell atop his head,
Zhengjue said, "If you wish to know Xuansha, he is simply a man pushing a dirt cart in a village of three households.
Fohai said, "The pattern of Xuefeng’s seamless stupa cannot be traced, nor can it be painted."
Just as he was about to do so, Xuansha exchanged it for a small clay pagoda.
[Later,] a monk asked Master Mingzhao, "How is it when the lion has not yet emerged from its cave? Mingzhao said, "A swift hawk cannot catch up.
The monk asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the cave? Mingzhao said, "Ten thousand miles of swirling dust. The monk said, "It wishes to emerge..."
"How is it before it has emerged? Zhao said, "Perilous. The monk asked, "How is it after it has gone forth? Zhao said, "Exiled. Fuguo commented:
"Since you have let go, you must know how to hold fast; since you have held fast, you must let go.
If someone were to suddenly ask Jiangshan today, 'How is it when the lion has not yet emerged from its den? I would answer him: 'Hidden.'"

"His fangs are bared and his claws extended; what is it like after he has emerged from the cave? He replied, "The grass bows and the wind blows. "What is it like when he is about to emerge but has not yet emerged?
He replied, "The cliffs collapse and the rocks split. "How is it when he has gone forth? He replied, "Flowers laid upon brocade."
Zhengjue said: "The old man Mingzhao rides a boat and runs on horseback; he has escaped death by a hair's breadth. It startles those who look on.
He has won through long practice; it spans thousands of miles."
The Buddha-ocean cloud drifts away with the current; it is gathered back by cutting through the waves. Tell me, is this a word from within the cave, or a word from outside the cave?
If you can discern this, I grant that you possess the claws and fangs of one who truly crouches upon the ground.
Master Shuangfeng was once ascending the hall and said: "To take one step forward is to lose the principle; to retreat one step is to lose the fact.
Even if you were to stand motionless and still, you would be no different from the insentient. At that time, a monk asked: "How can one avoid being the same as the insentient? Shuangfeng replied:
"By moving, turning, acting, and functioning. The monk asked: "How can one avoid losing the principle and missing the fact?"
The matter was over. Feng said, "Step forward; step back. The monk bowed. Feng said, "In the past, there were those who understood it in this way, but I did not approve of them.
The monk said, "I beg the Master to point it out directly. Feng then struck him.
Foguo held up his whisk and said: "A hawk seizing a swallow; like a falcon carrying off a pigeon. The subtlest of the subtle, the most wondrous of the wondrous.
To take one step forward, one does not lose sight of principle; to take one step back, one does not fail in regard to phenomena.
This is what is meant by 'in the midst of suchness, it is not suchness; in the midst of non-suchness, it is indeed suchness. Among these, this is the very last stroke of light."
The former is severed and the latter cut off.
Zhengjue said: "A cart does not push sideways. This monk comes in such a manner; the principle is not to be adjudged with crookedness.
I do not permit you to understand it in this way. Why? Because there are eyes upon the tip of the staff."
Buddha-Samudra-Cloud: When the ancients spoke in such a manner, they were merely striking the grass to startle the snake.
Here at Jiangshan, there are few who buy or sell. To speak directly: to take one step forward, there is no principle that is not so; to take one step back, there is no circumstance that is not right.
Standing thus motionless, whether in heaven or among men—if someone should suddenly prostrate themselves, I would simply point toward—
The Way. There have been those in the past who did not understand it in this way; I, the old monk, deeply approve of them.
But tell me, how far apart are they from the ancients? They are two colors and one match.
Buddha-Mirror, Buddha-Fruit, Perfect Enlightenment, Buddha-Ocean: Excerpts from the *Jewel Collection of the Eight Directions*, Part Two (End).
The *Jewel Collection of the Eight Directions* had been lost for sixty years.

Now, the various descendants of the later generation have exerted their collective efforts to carve this woodblock edition, establishing it permanently at Tianchi Monastery so that the source of the Dharma may be transmitted far and wide.
Recorded with reverence on a fine day in the eighth month of the year Yi-chou of the Zhide era.
